# Quantum Index

Quantum Index is a source-aware map of quantum theory and adjacent fundamental physics: historical foundations, formulations, interpretations, quantum field theories, information-theoretic frameworks, quantum gravity, quantum cosmology, astroparticle/cosmological models, quantum matter, quantum chemistry, AMO, and alternatives beyond standard quantum mechanics.

## Product goals

- Index quantum theories and major formulations past and present.
- Show lineage: what each idea extended, replaced, challenged, or unified.
- Make overlap visible instead of forcing every idea into one category.
- Separate **established framework**, **interpretation**, **active research program**, **historical/absorbed theory**, and **speculative alternative**.
- Preserve provenance so catalog coverage and source coverage are never confused.
- Support "thought trees": trace ancestors, descendants, rival branches, and cross-links.

## Current build

<!-- coverage:start -->
The census remains **open**. The current catalog contains **483 entries**, **614 typed relationships**, **41 thought trees**, and **601 bibliography records** across **14 categories**. Provenance is attached to all entries: **354 primary-sourced** and **129 review-sourced**. The formula atlas contains **457 entries** across **30 categories**; **114** theory entries remain documented formula gaps. Research depth currently includes **62** reading profiles, **35** Theory Passports, **9** scientific Problems, **21** Evidence records and **60** structured Research Questions. The reviewed development timeline contains **16** events through **2026**. Counts are generated from runtime data, separately from scientific review.
<!-- coverage:end -->

Static app:
- `index.html`
- `styles.css`
- `theories.js` — theory + relation catalog
- `formulas.js` — source-linked quantum formula atlas with equation-role metadata
- `formula-audit.js` — theory-by-theory formula-bearing coverage audit
- `profiles.js` — cited reading profiles and guided learning paths
- `workspace.js` — local research notes, bookmarks, progress and backup validation
- `app.js` — search, filters, graph, timeline, lineage, formula, comparison and workspace UI

## Data model

Each theory has:
- canonical name and aliases
- approximate first year / era
- category and status
- concise description and core claim
- tags
- provenance state
- relation graph

Relations are typed:
- `precursor`
- `reformulates`
- `extends`
- `challenges`
- `interprets`
- `unifies`
- `supports`
- `generalizes`
- `overlaps`

## Provenance rule

A catalogued theory is not automatically "fully sourced." The UI displays a provenance badge. Entries marked `catalogued` have been placed in the ontology but still require a dedicated source pass. Entries marked `review-sourced` have dedicated review/authoritative provenance; entries marked `primary-sourced` have at least one verified original or program-defining source attached.

## Development

No application build step is required. For development checks, run `npm ci`, `npm test`, and `npm run validate`. Run `npm run coverage` after catalog changes to regenerate coverage reports, then `npm run assets` after changes to shipped scripts or styles. CI verifies content-hashed asset URLs to prevent mixed cached releases. Test dependencies are development-only.

Theory links use `#/theory/<id>` and work on GitHub Pages without server routing.

 Open `index.html` or serve the repository as static files. GitHub Pages is deployed through the repository's native Pages configuration; catalog/formula integrity is enforced separately by `.github/workflows/validate.yml`.


## Research controls

See:
- `docs/COVERAGE.md` for current coverage, provenance metrics, gaps and completion criteria.
- `docs/TAXONOMY.md` for category, kind, status and relation semantics.
- `docs/FORMULA_AUDIT.md` for the theory-by-theory formula-bearing audit and formula-gap controls.
- `docs/RELATION_PROVENANCE.md` for edge-evidence semantics and the relation-source audit.
- `research/CANDIDATES.md` for the unresolved candidate backlog.
- `research/CANDIDATE_AUDIT.md` for add/alias/subtype/formula-only/duplicate decisions on remaining candidates.
- `research/EXHAUSTIVENESS_AUDIT.md` for the 2026-09-22 breadth census, acceptance criteria, and remaining lower-granularity queues.

The application must not describe the catalog as literally complete until the documented completeness acceptance criteria are satisfied. Unsourced candidates remain in the research backlog rather than entering the shipped catalog.


## Formula atlas

The formula atlas is a separate evidence layer linked to the theory graph. It contains canonical equations, identities, inequalities, Hamiltonians, spectra and topological relations. Current counts are generated in the census above. Every formula must link to at least one indexed theory and at least one existing source record.

"All formulas" is treated operationally rather than literally: quantum physics admits arbitrarily many derived equations, equivalent rearrangements, special cases and model-specific identities. The completeness target is therefore **all materially distinct, named or canonical formulas used to define, derive, test, or operationalize indexed quantum theories**, with variants tracked explicitly when they carry different physical content.

See:
- `docs/FORMULA_COVERAGE.md` for scope and current coverage.
- `research/FORMULA_CANDIDATES.md` for the next equation/formula sweeps.


## Formula governance

The formula atlas is deliberately scoped to **canonical/source-linked equations**, not every algebraic expression ever published. Each formula records:
- role: `exact`, `defining`, `canonical`, `schematic`, `approximation`, `limit`, or `derived identity`;
- assumptions;
- variables;
- applicable regime;
- units/dimensional notes;
- theory-to-formula relationship;
- source IDs and metadata review state.

`formula-audit.js` classifies every theory as formula-bearing, a documented formula gap, primarily conceptual, theorem, interpretation, or thought experiment. A documented gap means a canonical equation has not yet been curated; it does **not** mean the theory lacks mathematics.


## Relationship provenance

Every relation edge now carries:

- `sourceIds`
- `evidenceType`
- `confidence`
- optional `evidenceNote`

The first provenance pass source-backs the highest-confidence historical and formal edges. Unsourced edges are **explicitly labeled editorial** rather than silently presented as documented historical fact. This distinction is shown in theory details and graph tooltips.

Current relation evidence states are:
- `documented historical influence`
- `formal mathematical relation`
- `editorial relation`

Confidence is `high`, `medium`, or `editorial`.

## Learning and personal research

The Learn tab offers five guided paths, including Quantum foundations and Quantum information. Read markers show your progress, and Start/Continue/Review links in Learn and My research open the first unread step or return to the beginning when every entry is marked read. Gravity and time starts with a cited proper-time primer, and every path step has a reading profile. The Compare tab searches all catalog entries by name, alias or tag and compares two to four selections. Fifty-nine entries have expanded profiles; other entries retain their catalog summary and bibliography.

My research stores bookmarks, notes, read markers and saved comparisons in this browser only. Save notes explicitly. Export a JSON backup before clearing browser data or moving devices. Imports show a preview and merge with existing work; conflicting notes are appended rather than replaced. Limits are 20,000 characters per note, 100 saved comparisons and 1 MB per backup. Corrupt stored data is preserved and can be exported for recovery; storage failures do not report success. There is no account or cross-device synchronization.

Global filters apply to Network map, Timeline and Catalog. Comparisons and the formula atlas have their own controls. Graph and thought-tree nodes support Enter and Space.

The September 26 workspace release also reviews 25 existing graph edges in `docs/RELATION_REVIEW_2026-09-26.json`. Relationship disclosures expose the explanation, locator and sources. Source-backed does not mean experimentally confirmed.

My research also searches saved entries by name, alias, tag or full note text and saved comparisons by name or included entry. The Read entries list opens any marked entry, including entries outside learning paths. Search stays in place while visiting a detail and returning. Export research notebook downloads a Markdown reading copy with complete notes, entry links, catalog sources and comparison links; it always includes the whole workspace and does not replace the restorable JSON backup. Notes are exported as literal text.

The Coverage tab reports profile, formula and relationship review gaps from current data. URL filters survive reloads; relationship evidence and formula metadata review can be filtered separately. Draft notes survive navigation and tab reloads; conflicting cross-tab saves require explicit combination. See [the reliability release notes](docs/RELEASE_RELIABILITY_2026-09-27.md) for storage limits, browser CI and the Pages gate activation requirement.

### Structured comparison

Compare uses curated Theory Passports when available, including their assumptions, fundamental objects, regimes, linked scientific Problems, Evidence and Research Questions. Earlier cited profiles remain available in each comparison cell. Entries without a Passport keep their existing profile or explicit coverage gap; no profile is fabricated to fill a column. Comparison links, selection limits and browser-local saved comparisons are unchanged.

## Lattice-model curation

Three lattice-model Theory Passports (SSH, Aubry–André and Holstein) extend the original ten hubs, with five source-located representative equations and per-record review dates. The static SSH limit, ideal quasiperiodic model and quantum-phonon model are not treated as interchangeable. See `docs/RELEASE_LATTICE_CURATION_2026-10-07.md` for mathematical checks, preservation boundaries and release verification requirements.

## Current implementation: inspectable research navigation and foundational source audit

This follow-on implementation audits those fifteen foundation records against four inspected authoritative lecture-note references. It preserves their IDs, equations and theory links, distinguishes retained historical provenance from newly inspected sources, and promotes only the reviewed metadata to explicit status. This is equation-level documentation, not primary-original-source verification or empirical validation.

The atlas still has 457 formulas and 114 representative-formula gaps. This release adds no theory, formula or Evidence records. It adds a sixth editorial learning path, from primordial fluctuations through transfer physics to conditional CMB and large-scale-structure inference, reusing existing Evidence and Problems. Two explicitly qualified directed relations are documented; the study-step order does not generate graph edges.

Network now offers a source-backed directed-path search using the same pure engine as the CLI. It respects stored direction, shows every source locator, excludes editorial fallback and reports bounded no-path or zero-edge results honestly. Coverage adds factual record-level provenance, formula-review, Passport, Evidence and relationship inspection. Neither tool awards a scientific validity score or treats a path as proof.

Release verification requires independent review, current-runtime and historical-integrity tests, exact-head Chromium/WebKit checks, merged-main CI, Pages deployment and served-file verification. Consult the implementation pull request’s acceptance receipt for exact commits, run results and hosted verification; these instructions do not assert publication of an unverified revision. Dated historical ledgers remain unchanged. The separate academic-roadmap PR87 remains untouched and is not part of this release.

Subsequent scientific priorities are the remaining documented formula gaps, exact source-depth review of baseline metadata, qualified observational updates and deferred framework dispositions. Exploratory hypotheses belong in a separate research record until evidence supports catalog inclusion.

# Formula-bearing theory audit

_Last reviewed: 2026-09-22_

## Scope

This audit does **not** attempt to collect every algebraic expression ever derived in quantum physics. For every shipped entity it asks whether at least one canonical/source-linked equation is present, or whether the absence is explicitly classified.

The runtime audit is `formula-audit.js`; formula records are in `formulas.js`.

## Current result

<!-- coverage:start -->
- **62** cited reading profiles and **7** learning paths
- **35** Theory Passports, **9** scientific Problems, **21** Evidence records and **60** structured Research Questions
- **483** theory/framework entities across **14** categories
- **601** bibliography records
- **354** primary-sourced; **129** review-sourced; **0** catalogued-only entries
- **614** relationships: **130** source-backed; **484** editorial
- **41** thought trees
- **457** formulas across **30** categories
- **323** entries with linked formulas; **114** documented formula gaps
- Other audit classes: **11** interpretations, **16** conceptual, **18** theorem-first, **1** thought experiment
- Formula metadata: **265** explicitly reviewed; **192** baseline records
- **16** reviewed DevelopmentEvents through **2026**

Source attachment and formula presence are structural coverage measures, not verification of every claim or complete mathematical coverage.
<!-- coverage:end -->

A `formula-bearing-gap` is an explicit curation gap. It does not claim that the theory lacks mathematics.

## 2026-10-11 formula candidate reconciliation

The currently shipped atlas has **405** unique formula IDs. The separate `research/formula-candidates.json` curation ledger has **50** named candidates: **15 represented**, **13 partial**, **22 open**. Every linked formula ID in that ledger resolves to a shipped record at main `e1520a6c4b09cd425629825038dd0e190878024d`. These flags indicate representation scope, not full source/metadata validation; even an `open` candidate can reference a related but insufficient equation. The candidate ledger's September 27 reviewed date and historical proposal history are preserved.

The current gap count of **163** is entry-level; it cannot be subtracted from the 50 candidate rows because these use different units of analysis. **255** formula records still carry baseline metadata rather than an explicit source-location review. Next batches should inspect current gaps and baseline records by exact theory/formula ID, preserving equations already reviewed.

## Why the gap count increased

Theory breadth was expanded before formula curation. The third wave adds 50 source-backed frameworks without fabricating equations merely to keep the formula metric low. Of those additions, 49 enter as explicit formula-bearing gaps and the ABJ anomaly enters as theorem-first.

## Highest-priority formula closure domains

1. **Astroparticle physics & cosmology** — ΛCDM background equations/parameterization, freeze-in/freeze-out yields, neutrino-matter mixing, baryogenesis/leptogenesis, dark-sector field equations.
2. **Modified gravity** — Brans–Dicke, f(R), Horndeski, DHOST, DGP, dRGT, Einstein–Æther and Galileon defining actions/equations.
3. **Black-hole information** — Bekenstein–Hawking entropy/temperature linkage, JT action, complementarity/firewall entropy relations, BMV witness Hamiltonians where convention-safe.
4. **Canonical many-body models** — Bose–Hubbard, Heisenberg/Ising/Kitaev/AKLT, Luttinger/Fermi liquid, Bethe equations, SPT/topological-superconductor invariants.
5. **Electronic structure** — Born–Oppenheimer separation, CASSCF/CASPT2/NEVPT2, EOM-CC, ADC, GF2, DMET and DMRG-SCF.
6. **AMO** — Dicke/Tavis–Cummings, Floquet quasienergy, Rydberg blockade, EIT/STIRAP, optomechanical and optical-lattice Hamiltonians.

## Formula metadata schema

Every formula exposes:

- `formulaType`: `exact`, `defining`, `canonical`, `schematic`, `approximation`, `limit`, or `derived identity`
- assumptions
- variables
- regime
- units
- theory relationship
- metadata-review state
- linked theory IDs
- linked source IDs

## Acceptance rules

1. Every shipped theory must have exactly one audit entry.
2. Every `formula-bearing` theory must link at least one shipped formula.
3. Every `formula-bearing-gap` must carry a reason.
4. Every formula must link at least one theory and at least one catalogued source.
5. Schematic or approximate expressions must be labeled as such.
6. Formula coverage and theory coverage are reported separately.
7. Breadth expansion must never be blocked merely to keep the formula-gap count cosmetically low.

## Operational completeness target

A literal list of every quantum formula is not finite in a useful sense. Quantum Index targets **materially distinct named or canonical equations used to define, derive, test or operationalize indexed theories**.

Included classes:

1. defining Hamiltonians, Lagrangians, actions and evolution equations;
2. canonical spectra, inequalities, conservation laws and uncertainty relations;
3. standard measurement, information and entropy formulas;
4. canonical correlation functions, propagators and RG equations;

Trivial algebraic rearrangements stay out unless the variant carries different physical assumptions or regime.

A formula may enter the shipped atlas only if it has a stable ID, documented notation/regime, at least one linked theory, at least one linked source, a valid formula type, and no merely cosmetic duplication of an existing entry.

# Research profiles and comparison

Fifty-nine profiles in `profiles.js` cover historical foundations, quantum formulations, interpretations and no-go theorems, quantum information, open systems, quantum fields in spacetime, quantum-gravity approaches, black-hole information and primordial fluctuations, nuclear theory, chemistry, many-body physics, AMO, astroparticle models and beyond-standard correlations. Each has seven cited explanatory fields, a review date and an editorial prerequisite list. Questions are prompts for investigation, not a claim that every formulation remains unresolved in all models. Evidence descriptions concern the cited publications, not an exhaustive current experimental-status review.

The Compare tab accepts any two to four catalog entries. Three presets provide starting points. Each selector can search names, aliases and tags while retaining its current selection. Uncurated entries retain their catalog summaries, bibliography and formula coverage with an explicit missing-profile message. Selection is stored in the URL; theory links preserve the comparison return URL across reloads. Invalid IDs and duplicates are discarded; at most four valid IDs are retained.

<!-- coverage:start -->
- **62** cited reading profiles and **7** guided learning paths
- **35** Theory Passports available to the comparison workflow
- **483** catalog entries; **457** formula records; **601** bibliography records
- **614** typed relationships, including **130** source-backed edges

These counts are generated from runtime data; older release notes retain their historical snapshots.
<!-- coverage:end -->

Original IDs are preserved; subsequent equation-level metadata and bibliography corrections are documented in the release notes. Profile prerequisites do not create graph edges. The current typography and colors are reused; comparison columns scroll horizontally when needed.

Validation includes profile citations and identifiers, presets, navigation, selection limits, uncurated-entry fallback, all profile rendering, and fresh comparison/detail loads. Browser checks complement DOM tests; a real narrow viewport must be checked separately before claiming mobile verification.

Source basis: the linked original papers and reviews, including their abstracts and selected accessible text. These concise profiles are reading aids, not exhaustive literature reviews. Older papers are identified by their citation dates and do not establish present-day experimental status.

## Guided learning paths

The Learning paths tab provides five editorial routes: Gravity and time, The black-hole information problem, Approaches to quantum gravity, Quantum foundations, and Quantum information. Each route lists background knowledge, ordered reading prompts, read/not-read indicators, previous/next steps and a concluding comparison. Progress bars and Start/Continue/Review links appear in both Learn and My research. Continue chooses the first unread step, including skipped earlier entries. Review from start leaves all read markers intact. Shared entries count toward every path that includes them; progress stays browser-local and travels with exported/imported read markers. Route URLs and their theory-step URLs retain path context on reload. Unknown path IDs show the complete path list. These routes reuse existing catalog entries and do not introduce historical graph relationships. Every step has an expanded profile. Gravity and time begins with a sourced primer distinguishing proper time, Schwarzschild clock rates and the Unruh effect.

`docs/responsive-check.html` is a manual QA page that embeds the actual application at 320, 390 or 430 CSS pixels. It exercises responsive rendering without claiming device or Safari emulation.

## Personal research and release checks

My research supports browser-local bookmarks, explicitly saved notes, read markers and saved comparisons. JSON export/import includes validation, a merge preview, preservation of conflicting notes and explicit storage-failure reporting. See `WORKSPACE_RELEASE_2026-09-26.md` for limits and verification evidence.

PR #44 passed all 35 tests and Pages deployment. Live checks verified the 50-profile collection, searchable comparison, prerequisite return URLs, learning context after reload, all three new equations rendered by MathJax, and persisted bookmarks/notes/read markers. A real exported JSON backup was downloaded and parsed successfully. After resetting a stalled browser-control session, the actual exported backup was imported, merged and verified after reload. Saved comparison behavior also passed. The 320/390/430-pixel checks found one native file-picker overflow in the 320-pixel workspace; the follow-up constrains that label and input to the available width. Other views fit at all three widths. Automated import preview, merge and malformed-backup checks pass. Physical iPhone/Safari testing was not available.

## September 27 reliability and depth pass

Nine new cross-domain profiles bring every category into the profile collection. Automated Chromium and mobile WebKit tests cover note conflicts, draft recovery, durable URLs, rendered equations and 320-pixel layout. WebKit emulation does not replace physical iPhone testing. Current counts and remaining research gaps appear in [Coverage](COVERAGE.md).

index.html.beforeText:
Q

Quantum Index

Source-aware map of fundamental physics.

FUNDAMENTAL PHYSICS ATLAS

Explore the ideas shaping modern physics.

Move through theories, equations, evidence, historical lineage and open research while keeping the source trail visible.

Search and filters update the Network map, Timeline and Catalog.

START WITH YOUR QUESTION

Choose how you want to explore fundamental physics

Move from scientific problems to competing approaches, equations, evidence, recent developments, research questions and primary literature.

WHAT'S NEW

Recent reviewed developments

Full development timeline

OPEN RESEARCH

Questions still requiring work

All open questions

Upstream and downstream show typed connections, not necessarily historical causation. The filter also applies to theory connections and thought trees.

RELATIONSHIP GRAPH

Ideas as a connected system

Drag nodes. Scroll to zoom. Select a node for lineage, status, overlaps and related ideas.

← Back to network map

ORIGINS + DEVELOPMENTS

Timeline of fundamental physics

Theory origins remain historical; later developments keep their own dates.

THOUGHT TREES

Major intellectual branches

Choose a branch. The map uses the catalog's actual typed relationships; it does not invent arrows between adjacent items.

PROGRESSION MAP

Thought tree

100%

Zoom with + and −, then drag the background or scroll to pan. Focus the map for arrow keys, +/− and 0 to fit. Select a node to inspect it below; Open full details opens its page.

Horizontal position is chronological. Rows show primary catalog category. Arrows appear only for relationships explicitly stored in the index.

SELECTED LINEAGE

Choose a theory

Select a node to inspect its upstream ideas, downstream progression and overlaps.

INDEX

All catalogued theories

SCIENTIFIC PROBLEMS

Start with the question physics is trying to answer

Problems organize existing theories, formulas, evidence, developments and research questions without turning the problem itself into a theory.

EVIDENCE + CONSTRAINTS

What experiments and observations actually establish

Each record separates the measured result from the theories or parameter space it constrains—and from conclusions it does not establish.

RESEARCH QUESTIONS

What is established, conditional, model-specific or still open?

These records preserve the reviewed 59-question profile audit and add focused problem-level questions as new literature is reviewed. They are research-orientation summaries, not declarations that every prompt is an unsolved problem.

COMPARE APPROACHES

Explore the differences

Choose two to four entries. Compare their scope, assumptions, results and limitations. A source citation is not a verdict of experimental confirmation.

Permanent comparison link

CURATED RESEARCH GUIDES

Foundations, information and gravity

Expanded research profiles with suggested prerequisites. These reading suggestions are not additional historical connections in the graph.

EQUATION INDEX

Quantum formula atlas

Canonical equations, identities, bounds and model Hamiltonians linked back to the theories and sources that use them.

On quantumindex.site, Cloudflare Web Analytics measures site visits, referrers and page performance without analytics cookies. It does not receive your research notes or saved workspace. Hash-based tabs and search terms are not reported as separate pages. About Cloudflare Web Analytics.

window.QI_DATA = (() => {
  // Chronological eras follow the recorded first year, not a later resurgence.
  const eraForYear = year => year < 1900 ? "Before 1900" : year < 1925 ? "1900–1924" : year < 1940 ? "1925–1939" : year < 1960 ? "1940–1959" : year < 1980 ? "1960–1979" : year < 2000 ? "1980–1999" : year < 2015 ? "2000–2014" : "2015–present";
  const T = (id,name,year,era,category,status,summary,core,tags=[],aliases=[],kind=null) => ({
    id,name,year,era:eraForYear(year),category,status,summary,core,tags,aliases,
    kind: kind || (
      status === "interpretation" ? "interpretation" :
      category === "Formulations" ? "formulation" :
      category === "Historical foundations" ? "historical framework" :
      category === "Quantum field theory" ? "theory / framework" :
      category === "Quantum gravity & spacetime" ? "research program" :
      category === "Quantum cosmology" ? "cosmological framework" :
      category === "Mathematical structures" ? "mathematical framework" :
      category === "Beyond standard quantum theory" ? "alternative / extension" :
      "framework"
    ),
    provenance:"catalogued",sources:[],lastReviewed:null
  });

  const theories = [
    T("ssh-model","Su–Schrieffer–Heeger model",1979,"","Quantum many-body & condensed matter","established","An electron–lattice model of polyacetylene with alternating bonds and soliton domain walls; its fixed-dimerization limit is the SSH chain.","Bond-dependent hopping couples electronic motion to lattice distortion.",["SSH", "dimerization", "solitons", "electron-phonon"],["Su-Schrieffer-Heeger model", "SSH chain"],"model"),
    T("aubry-andre","Aubry–André quasiperiodic localization model",1980,"","Quantum many-body & condensed matter","established","A one-dimensional lattice model with an incommensurate onsite modulation, used to study localization without a random potential.","Quasiperiodic modulation competes with hopping and supports a localization transition in the ideal model.",["Aubry-André", "quasiperiodic", "localization"],["Aubry-Andre model", "Aubry–André–Harper model"],"model"),
    T("holstein-model","Holstein molecular-crystal / polaron model",1959,"","Quantum many-body & condensed matter","established","A tight-binding electron couples to local molecular vibrations, providing a model of electron–phonon dressing and polaron motion.","Local electronic occupancy shifts local vibrational coordinates.",["Holstein", "polaron", "electron-phonon"],["Holstein model", "molecular-crystal model"],"model"),
    T("deconfined-criticality","Deconfined quantum criticality",2003,"","Quantum many-body & condensed matter","active research","A proposed description of certain quantum critical points using fractionalized degrees of freedom and emergent gauge fields instead of only conventional order parameters.","Fractionalized fields can become the effective critical variables between phases with conventional order.",["DQCP", "spinons", "emergent gauge fields"],["Deconfined quantum critical points"],"critical framework"),
    T("fracton-phases","Fracton phases and restricted-mobility frameworks",2004,"","Quantum many-body & condensed matter","active research","Frameworks for excitations whose motion is constrained under local operations. The date marks Chamon’s early model; the broader fracton terminology developed later.","Individual excitations can be immobile or restricted to subdimensions even when composites can move.",["fracton", "restricted mobility", "tensor gauge theory"],["Fracton order", "Fracton matter"],"phase framework"),
    T("quantum-many-body-scars","Quantum many-body scar framework",2017,"","Quantum many-body & condensed matter","active research","Atypical nonthermal eigenstates embedded in an otherwise thermalizing spectrum can produce long-lived revivals for selected initial states.","Weak ergodicity breaking can arise from special eigenstates without localizing the whole spectrum.",["quantum scars", "PXP", "weak ergodicity breaking"],["Many-body quantum scars", "Quantum many-body scars"],"dynamical framework"),
    T("discrete-time-crystals","Discrete / Floquet time-crystal framework",2016,"","Quantum many-body & condensed matter","active research","Driven many-body phases can spontaneously break discrete time-translation symmetry, giving a robust response with a period longer than the drive.","Time-translation symmetry breaking distinguishes the phase from ordinary forced oscillations.",["time crystal", "Floquet", "subharmonic response"],["Discrete time crystals", "Floquet time crystals"],"nonequilibrium phase framework"),
    T("measurement-induced-transition","Measurement-induced entanglement transitions",2018,"","Quantum many-body & condensed matter","active research","Hybrid circuits combining unitary gates and measurements can exhibit transitions between volume-law and area-law entanglement in conditioned trajectories.","Measurement and unitary evolution compete in the entanglement structure of individual quantum trajectories.",["hybrid circuits", "measurement-induced", "entanglement transition"],["Measurement-induced phase transition", "MIPT"],"dynamical phase-transition framework"),
    T("quantum-discord","Quantum discord framework",2001,"","Quantum information & open systems","established","A measurement-dependent difference between quantum mutual-information expressions characterizes correlations beyond a purely classical description.","Local measurement generally changes the accessible correlation information.",["discord", "quantum correlations", "mutual information"],["Quantum discord"],"correlation framework"),
    T("coherence-resource-theory","Resource theory of quantum coherence",2013,"","Quantum information & open systems","active research","A resource framework relative to a chosen reference basis, with incoherent states and specified free operations used to quantify coherence.","Coherence measures must respect the selected class of incoherent operations.",["coherence", "incoherent operations", "resource theory"],["Quantum coherence resource theory"],"resource framework"),
    T("quantum-zeno","Quantum Zeno effect and dynamics",1977,"","Quantum information & open systems","established","Sufficiently frequent measurements can inhibit transitions or constrain evolution to a measurement subspace under appropriate conditions.","The measurement protocol and short-time quantum dynamics determine the Zeno limit.",["Zeno", "repeated measurement", "measurement dynamics"],["Quantum Zeno effect", "Quantum Zeno dynamics"],"measurement dynamics"),
    T("berry-phase","Berry phase / adiabatic geometric phase",1984,"","Mathematical structures","established","An adiabatically transported eigenstate acquires a geometric phase associated with its path through Hamiltonian parameter space.","Connection and curvature describe geometry beyond the dynamical phase for an isolated eigenstate.",["Berry phase", "geometric phase", "adiabatic"],["Adiabatic geometric phase", "Berry-phase framework"],"geometric framework"),
    T("aharonov-bohm","Aharonov–Bohm effect framework",1959,"","Quantum optics & AMO","established","Charged-particle interference can depend on enclosed magnetic flux even when the particle paths lie in a field-free region.","The observable phase difference is gauge invariant and depends on the closed-path electromagnetic holonomy.",["Aharonov-Bohm", "flux", "interference"],["Aharonov-Bohm effect", "AB effect"],"interference effect"),
    T("fano-resonance","Fano discrete–continuum resonance theory",1961,"","Quantum optics & AMO","established","Interference involving a discrete state coupled to a continuum produces asymmetric resonance profiles in excitation and scattering.","The resonant and continuum excitation pathways interfere.",["Fano", "autoionization", "resonance"],["Fano resonance", "Fano interference"],"resonance framework"),
    T("quantum-steering","Operational quantum steering framework",2006,"","Quantum information & open systems","established","A formalization of Schrödinger’s 1935 steering idea tests whether bipartite correlations admit a local hidden-state description for the trusted party.","Steerability occupies a distinct place between entanglement and Bell nonlocality under the stated measurement scenario.",["EPR steering", "local hidden state", "one-sided trust"],["Quantum steering", "EPR steering"],"correlation framework"),
    T("quantum-kibble-zurek","Quantum Kibble–Zurek framework",2005,"","Quantum many-body & condensed matter","active research","Finite-rate sweeps across a quantum critical point produce nonadiabatic excitations whose scaling can be related to critical dynamics.","Critical slowing down limits adiabatic following during a quantum quench.",["Kibble-Zurek", "quantum quench", "defect scaling"],["Quantum Kibble-Zurek mechanism"],"nonequilibrium scaling framework"),

    T("density-operator","Density-operator formulation",1927,"1925–1939","Formulations","established","The density operator generalizes pure quantum states to statistical mixtures and reduced subsystem states.","Quantum states may be represented by positive trace-one operators, with expectation values computed by the trace rule.",["density matrix","mixed states","trace"],["density-matrix formalism"],"formulation"),
    T("canonical-quantization","Canonical quantization",1926,"1925–1939","Formulations","established framework","Canonical quantization promotes classical canonical variables to noncommuting operators obeying quantum commutation relations.","Classical Poisson-bracket structure is mapped, subject to ordering and domain issues, into operator commutators on a quantum state space.",["quantization","commutators","Hamiltonian"],[],"quantization framework"),
    T("quantum-logic","Birkhoff–von Neumann quantum logic",1936,"1925–1939","Foundations & interpretations","established framework","Quantum logic studies the non-Boolean logical structure formed by propositions represented by subspaces or projectors in Hilbert space.","The lattice of quantum propositions is generally non-distributive, motivating alternatives to classical propositional logic for quantum events.",["quantum logic","projectors","lattice","Birkhoff","von Neumann"],[],"formal framework"),
    T("wigner-friend","Wigner's friend",1961,"1960–1979","Foundations & interpretations","historical","Wigner's-friend scenarios expose tension between universal unitary evolution and definite measurement outcomes for nested observers.","An observer can assign a definite result while a larger external description treats the observer and measured system as a coherent quantum state.",["measurement problem","observer","thought experiment"],[],"thought experiment"),
    T("ontological-models","Ontological-models framework",2005,"2000–2014","Foundations & interpretations","active research","Ontological-model frameworks represent preparations, transformations and measurements through underlying ontic states in order to classify possible completions or explanations of quantum statistics.","Operational procedures are represented by probability distributions and response functions over an underlying state space, enabling precise tests of contextuality and ψ-ontology.",["ontological models","hidden variables","contextuality","psi ontology"],[],"formal framework"),
    T("generalized-contextuality","Generalized contextuality",2005,"2000–2014","Foundations & interpretations","active research","Spekkens generalized contextuality beyond sharp measurements to preparations, transformations and unsharp measurements using operational equivalences.","Operationally equivalent procedures must have identical ontological representations in a noncontextual model; quantum theory violates this in suitable scenarios.",["contextuality","Spekkens","operational equivalence"],[],"foundational framework"),
    T("spekkens-toy","Spekkens toy theory",2007,"2000–2014","Beyond standard quantum theory","toy model","A restricted-knowledge toy theory reproduces many qualitative quantum phenomena without being full quantum mechanics.","An epistemic restriction on knowledge of an underlying classical-like ontic state generates analogues of interference, no-cloning and entanglement-like correlations.",["psi epistemic","toy model","Spekkens","foundations"],[],"toy theory"),
    T("psi-ontology","ψ-ontic / ψ-epistemic framework",2007,"2000–2014","Foundations & interpretations","active research","The ψ-ontology framework classifies ontological models according to whether distinct quantum states correspond to overlapping or disjoint distributions of underlying physical states.","The status of the wavefunction is analyzed by the overlap structure of ontic-state distributions associated with different preparations.",["wavefunction","psi ontic","psi epistemic","ontological models"],[],"classification framework"),
    T("pbr-theorem","Pusey–Barrett–Rudolph theorem",2012,"2000–2014","Foundations & interpretations","established theorem","The PBR theorem constrains ψ-epistemic ontological models under a preparation-independence assumption.","If independently prepared systems have independent ontic states, distinct pure quantum states cannot correspond to overlapping ontic distributions in the way targeted by the theorem.",["PBR","psi ontology","no-go theorem"],[],"theorem"),
    T("leggett-garg","Leggett–Garg inequalities",1985,"1980–1999","Foundations & interpretations","established theorem","Leggett–Garg inequalities test combinations of macrorealism and noninvasive measurability using temporal correlations.","Certain temporal-correlation bounds must hold for a class of macrorealist descriptions and can be violated by quantum systems.",["macrorealism","temporal correlations","no-go theorem"],[],"theorem"),
    T("ithaca","Ithaca interpretation",1998,"1980–1999","Foundations & interpretations","interpretation","Mermin's Ithaca interpretation emphasizes objective correlations while refusing to assign fundamental status to correlata.","Correlations between subsystems are treated as physically real even when definite underlying values are not taken as fundamental.",["Mermin","correlations","interpretation"],[],"interpretation"),
    T("objective-collapse","Objective-collapse theories",1986,"1980–1999","Foundations & interpretations","alternative theory","Objective-collapse programs modify standard quantum dynamics so that state reduction is a real stochastic physical process.","Microscopic superpositions persist approximately while sufficiently macroscopic superpositions are dynamically suppressed without requiring observers.",["collapse","measurement problem","GRW","CSL"],[],"theory family"),

    T("wightman-qft","Wightman axiomatic QFT",1956,"1940–1959","Quantum field theory","established framework","Wightman QFT axiomatizes relativistic quantum fields as operator-valued distributions acting on a Hilbert space.","Covariance, spectrum conditions, vacuum structure and local commutativity constrain relativistic quantum fields independently of a particular perturbative Lagrangian calculation.",["Wightman","axiomatic QFT","locality","operator-valued distributions"],[],"axiomatic framework"),
    T("constructive-qft","Constructive quantum field theory",1960,"1960–1979","Quantum field theory","active research","Constructive QFT seeks mathematically rigorous interacting quantum field models rather than formal perturbative series alone.","Interacting models are built with controlled measures, correlation functions and continuum limits that satisfy rigorous field-theoretic requirements.",["constructive QFT","rigor","Euclidean fields"],[],"research program"),
    T("schwinger-keldysh","Schwinger–Keldysh / closed-time-path formalism",1961,"1960–1979","Formulations","established framework","The closed-time-path formalism extends field theory to nonequilibrium and real-time expectation values using forward and backward time contours.","Correlation functions are computed on a doubled time contour, allowing initial-value quantum dynamics and nonequilibrium response to be treated systematically.",["nonequilibrium","closed time path","Keldysh","Schwinger"],[],"formulation"),
    T("induced-gravity","Sakharov induced gravity",1967,"1960–1979","Quantum gravity & spacetime","active research","Induced-gravity programs explore whether gravitational dynamics arise as an effective response of quantum matter or vacuum degrees of freedom.","Einstein-like gravitational terms can emerge in an effective action generated by quantum fields rather than being fundamental microscopic terms.",["Sakharov","emergent gravity","effective action"],[],"research program"),
    T("geometric-quantization","Geometric quantization",1970,"1960–1979","Formulations","established framework","Geometric quantization constructs quantum Hilbert spaces and observables from symplectic classical phase spaces using line bundles and polarizations.","Classical symplectic geometry is lifted into quantum state-space structure through prequantization followed by a choice of polarization.",["symplectic geometry","quantization","polarization"],[],"quantization framework"),
    T("conformal-bootstrap","Conformal bootstrap",1970,"1960–1979","Quantum field theory","active research","The conformal bootstrap constrains or solves conformal field theories using symmetry, crossing consistency and unitarity rather than a specific microscopic Lagrangian.","Operator dimensions and OPE coefficients must satisfy self-consistency equations generated by conformal symmetry and crossing.",["bootstrap","CFT","crossing symmetry","unitarity"],[],"nonperturbative framework"),
    T("gksl","GKSL / Lindblad open-system dynamics",1976,"1960–1979","Quantum information & open systems","established framework","The Gorini–Kossakowski–Sudarshan–Lindblad structure characterizes Markovian completely positive trace-preserving quantum dynamical semigroups.","A density operator evolves under a generator containing Hamiltonian and dissipative terms constrained to preserve quantum-state consistency.",["Lindblad","GKSL","open systems","master equation"],[],"dynamical framework"),
    T("higher-derivative-qg","Higher-derivative quantum gravity",1977,"1960–1979","Quantum gravity & spacetime","active research","Higher-curvature gravitational actions add terms such as curvature-squared invariants to improve ultraviolet behavior.","Additional derivatives can make perturbative gravity power-counting renormalizable, while introducing difficult questions about extra modes and unitarity.",["Stelle gravity","higher derivatives","renormalization"],[],"quantum-gravity approach"),
    T("euclidean-qg","Euclidean quantum gravity",1978,"1960–1979","Quantum gravity & spacetime","active research","Euclidean quantum gravity studies gravitational path integrals after continuation to Riemannian-signature geometries.","Quantum amplitudes are approached through sums over Euclidean metrics, often as a formal or semiclassical tool despite convergence and contour issues.",["Euclidean gravity","path integral","instantons"],[],"quantum-gravity approach"),
    T("stochastic-quantization","Stochastic quantization",1981,"1980–1999","Formulations","active research","Parisi–Wu stochastic quantization introduces an auxiliary stochastic time so that equilibrium distributions reproduce Euclidean quantum field theory.","A classical stochastic process in one extra parameter can generate quantum-field correlation functions without conventional gauge fixing in some settings.",["Parisi-Wu","stochastic","quantization"],[],"quantization framework"),
    T("bv-formalism","Batalin–Vilkovisky formalism",1981,"1980–1999","Formulations","established framework","The BV formalism generalizes BRST methods to gauge theories with complex or open gauge algebras using an extended graded phase space.","Fields and antifields are organized so that the master equation encodes gauge symmetry and consistent quantization.",["BV","antifields","gauge theory","master equation"],[],"quantization framework"),
    T("brst","BRST quantization",1975,"1960–1979","Formulations","established framework","BRST symmetry provides a systematic method for quantizing gauge theories while controlling redundant gauge degrees of freedom.","Ghost fields and a nilpotent BRST charge encode gauge invariance in the quantum theory and identify physical states through cohomology.",["BRST","ghosts","gauge theory","cohomology"],[],"quantization framework"),
    T("quantum-regge","Quantum Regge calculus",1980,"1980–1999","Quantum gravity & spacetime","active research","Quantum Regge approaches discretize spacetime into simplices and attempt a gravitational path integral over edge lengths or related discrete data.","Piecewise-flat simplicial geometries replace smooth metrics as the variables summed over or quantized.",["Regge calculus","simplicial gravity","discrete spacetime"],[],"quantum-gravity approach"),
    T("third-quantization","Third quantization",1980,"1980–1999","Quantum cosmology","speculative","Third-quantized approaches promote the wavefunction of the universe itself to a field-like object on superspace.","Universes become excitations of a higher-level field theory, allowing creation and annihilation processes in superspace.",["third quantization","superspace","multiverse"],[],"cosmological framework"),
    T("string-gas-cosmology","String gas cosmology",1989,"1980–1999","Quantum cosmology","active research","String-gas cosmology studies early-universe dynamics of thermal ensembles of strings, including winding modes and string dualities.","String-specific degrees of freedom can alter high-temperature cosmology and the dynamical selection of large spatial dimensions.",["string cosmology","winding modes","T-duality"],[],"cosmological framework"),
    T("quantum-trajectories","Quantum trajectories / stochastic unravelings",1990,"1980–1999","Quantum information & open systems","established framework","Quantum-trajectory methods represent open-system master equations as ensembles of stochastic pure-state evolutions conditioned on measurement records or environmental events.","Different stochastic unravelings reproduce the same reduced density-operator evolution while describing distinct monitoring schemes.",["quantum trajectories","unraveling","open systems","continuous measurement"],[],"dynamical framework"),
    T("functional-rg","Functional renormalization group",1993,"1980–1999","Quantum field theory","active research","Functional RG methods evolve an effective action with a continuous scale parameter, enabling nonperturbative approximations to quantum field theories.","Exact flow equations such as the Wetterich equation describe how effective interactions change as fluctuations are integrated scale by scale.",["FRG","Wetterich equation","renormalization","nonperturbative"],[],"nonperturbative framework"),
    T("pr-box","PR-box / superquantum correlations",1994,"1980–1999","Beyond standard quantum theory","toy model","Popescu–Rohrlich correlations are hypothetical nonsignalling correlations stronger than those allowed by quantum mechanics.","They saturate the algebraic CHSH bound while preserving no-signalling, providing a benchmark for asking why quantum nonlocality is limited.",["PR box","non-signalling","post-quantum","CHSH"],[],"toy theory"),
    T("perturbative-aqft","Perturbative algebraic QFT",1996,"1980–1999","Quantum field theory","active research","Perturbative AQFT combines local algebraic QFT with causal perturbation theory to construct interacting observables without relying on a global vacuum representation.","Interacting local algebras are defined perturbatively using causal locality, microlocal analysis and renormalized time-ordered products.",["pAQFT","AQFT","causal perturbation theory"],[],"research framework"),
    T("doubly-special-relativity","Doubly special relativity",2001,"2000–2014","Quantum gravity & spacetime","speculative","DSR models deform relativistic kinematics so that, in addition to the speed of light, a high-energy or Planckian scale is observer-independent.","Lorentz transformations are modified or nonlinearly realized to accommodate an invariant energy or length scale.",["DSR","deformed relativity","Planck scale"],[],"quantum-spacetime model"),
    T("quantum-graphity","Quantum graphity",2006,"2000–2014","Quantum gravity & spacetime","speculative","Quantum graphity models treat adjacency or connectivity of a graph as quantum degrees of freedom from which low-energy geometry might emerge.","A highly connected pre-geometric quantum system can undergo phases whose graph structure resembles local spatial geometry.",["emergent spacetime","quantum graph","pregeometry"],[],"emergent-spacetime model"),
    T("quantum-combs","Quantum combs",2008,"2000–2014","Quantum information & open systems","established framework","Quantum combs provide an operator framework for multi-step quantum networks with memory and definite causal order.","A sequence of channels with open input/output slots is represented by a positive operator obeying normalization constraints.",["quantum networks","memory","higher-order maps"],[],"process framework"),
    T("quantum-switch","Quantum switch",2009,"2000–2014","Quantum information & open systems","active research","The quantum switch coherently controls the order in which two operations act on a target system.","A control degree of freedom can place alternative gate orders into quantum superposition, producing a higher-order quantum process.",["quantum switch","causal order","higher-order process"],[],"process framework"),
    T("relative-locality","Relative locality",2011,"2000–2014","Quantum gravity & spacetime","active research","Relative locality explores kinematics in which momentum space is curved and the localization of distant events becomes observer-dependent.","Nonlinear momentum composition and curved momentum-space geometry can make spacetime locality relative rather than absolute.",["relative locality","momentum space","Planck scale"],[],"quantum-spacetime framework"),
    T("generalized-uncertainty","Generalized uncertainty principle / minimal-length models",1995,"1980–1999","Quantum gravity & spacetime","speculative","GUP models modify canonical uncertainty or commutation relations to encode a minimum resolvable length near the Planck scale.","Planck-scale corrections can alter the relation between position and momentum uncertainties and modify high-energy kinematics.",["GUP","minimal length","Planck scale","quantum gravity phenomenology"],[],"phenomenological framework"),
    T("process-tensor","Process-tensor framework",2018,"2015–present","Quantum information & open systems","active research","Process tensors generalize quantum channels to multi-time open-system processes with memory and operational interventions.","A many-time quantum process maps sequences of control operations to outcome statistics while retaining temporal correlations and non-Markovian memory.",["process tensor","non-Markovian","multi-time","open systems"],[],"process framework"),
    T("minisuperspace","Minisuperspace quantum cosmology",1967,"1960–1979","Quantum cosmology","active research","Minisuperspace models truncate the infinite degrees of freedom of gravity to a finite set of homogeneous or symmetric cosmological variables before quantization.","The Wheeler–DeWitt equation becomes a finite-dimensional quantum constraint for variables such as the scale factor and homogeneous matter fields.",["minisuperspace","Wheeler-DeWitt","quantum cosmology"],[],"cosmological framework"),
    T("perturbative-qg","Perturbative quantum gravity",1963,"1960–1979","Quantum gravity & spacetime","effective framework","Perturbative quantum gravity expands the metric around a background and quantizes gravitational fluctuations as a spin-2 field.","At accessible energies it functions as an effective quantum field theory, while straightforward Einstein gravity is not perturbatively renormalizable as a fundamental UV theory.",["graviton","perturbation theory","effective field theory"],[],"quantum-gravity framework"),
    T("euclidean-qft","Euclidean QFT / Osterwalder–Schrader framework",1973,"1960–1979","Quantum field theory","established framework","Euclidean QFT formulates correlation functions in imaginary time, with Osterwalder–Schrader conditions linking suitable Euclidean theories back to relativistic Wightman QFT.","Reflection positivity and related axioms permit reconstruction of a Minkowski-space quantum field theory from Euclidean correlation functions.",["Osterwalder-Schrader","Euclidean QFT","reflection positivity"],[],"axiomatic framework"),
    T("real-qm","Real-Hilbert-space quantum theory",1960,"1960–1979","Beyond standard quantum theory","alternative framework","Real quantum theory replaces complex Hilbert spaces with real Hilbert spaces while retaining analogous state and measurement structures.","Restricting amplitudes to real numbers changes composition and information-theoretic properties even when many single-system predictions resemble complex quantum mechanics.",["real Hilbert space","alternative quantum theory","composition"],[],"alternative framework")
,
    T("jordan-algebra-qm","Jordan-algebraic quantum mechanics",1934,"1925–1939","Mathematical structures","active research","Jordan, von Neumann and Wigner explored a generalized quantum formalism based on commutative but generally nonassociative algebras of observables.","Quantum observables may be organized by a Jordan product rather than taking the full associative operator product as primitive.",["Jordan algebra","nonassociative","observables","foundations"],[],"alternative mathematical framework"),
    T("light-front-quantization","Light-front quantization",1949,"1940–1959","Formulations","established framework","Light-front quantization formulates relativistic quantum dynamics on null hypersurfaces rather than ordinary equal-time slices.","Quantum states evolve with a light-front time coordinate, changing which Poincaré generators are kinematical and dynamical.",["light front","front form","relativistic dynamics","quantization"],["front-form dynamics"],"quantization framework"),
    T("causal-perturbation","Epstein–Glaser causal perturbation theory",1973,"1960–1979","Quantum field theory","established framework","Causal perturbation theory constructs renormalized perturbative QFT distributions recursively from locality and causality without introducing divergent intermediate integrals.","Time-ordered products are extended to coincident points under causal factorization constraints, turning renormalization into a distribution-extension problem.",["Epstein-Glaser","renormalization","locality","perturbative QFT"],[],"quantization framework"),
    T("quantum-stochastic-calculus","Quantum stochastic calculus",1984,"1980–1999","Quantum information & open systems","established framework","Quantum stochastic calculus extends Itô calculus to noncommuting operator-valued noise processes and underlies continuous-time quantum input-output theory.","Bosonic field noises obey a noncommutative Itô table, enabling stochastic differential equations for open quantum systems.",["Hudson-Parthasarathy","quantum noise","Ito calculus","open systems"],[],"dynamical framework"),
    T("p-adic-qm","p-adic quantum mechanics",1989,"1980–1999","Beyond standard quantum theory","speculative","p-adic quantum mechanics explores quantum dynamics over p-adic number fields rather than only the real or complex numbers.","State amplitudes and evolution are reformulated using non-Archimedean p-adic analysis and additive characters.",["p-adic","non-Archimedean","number theory","alternative quantum theory"],[],"alternative framework"),
    T("q-deformed-qm","q-deformed quantum mechanics",1989,"1980–1999","Beyond standard quantum theory","active research","q-deformed quantum models replace ordinary oscillator or symmetry algebras with deformed quantum-group relations.","Creation, annihilation and symmetry operators obey q-dependent algebraic relations that reduce to familiar ones in an undeformed limit.",["q deformation","quantum groups","q oscillator","algebra"],[],"alternative framework"),
    T("tensor-network-states","Tensor-network / matrix-product-state framework",1992,"1980–1999","Quantum information & open systems","established framework","Tensor-network states compress many-body wavefunctions by factorizing their amplitudes into networks of low-rank tensors.","Entanglement structure is represented through contracted auxiliary indices, making important low-entanglement many-body states tractable.",["tensor networks","MPS","many-body","entanglement"],["matrix-product states","finitely correlated states"],"mathematical framework"),
    T("quantum-measure-theory","Quantum measure theory",1994,"1980–1999","Foundations & interpretations","active research","Quantum measure theory generalizes classical additive probability measures on histories to weaker quantum sum rules.","A generalized measure on sets of histories encodes interference while permitting formulations in which a single history is treated as physically real.",["quantum measure","histories","Sorkin","generalized probability"],[],"foundational framework"),
    T("topos-quantum","Topos approaches to quantum theory",1998,"1980–1999","Mathematical structures","active research","Topos approaches reformulate quantum propositions, valuations and contextuality using presheaves and intuitionistic logic.","Quantum observables and propositions are organized over contexts so that generalized valuations can exist despite Kochen–Specker obstructions.",["topos","presheaves","contextuality","quantum logic"],[],"mathematical framework"),
    T("causal-set-growth","Causal-set sequential growth dynamics",1999,"1980–1999","Quantum gravity & spacetime","active research","Sequential-growth models give causal sets a label-independent stochastic dynamics constrained by causality and discrete general covariance.","A causal set grows one element at a time with transition probabilities restricted by covariance and causal structure.",["causal sets","sequential growth","discrete covariance","stochastic dynamics"],[],"causal-set dynamics"),
    T("adiabatic-qc","Adiabatic quantum computation",2000,"2000–2014","Quantum information & open systems","established framework","Adiabatic quantum computation encodes a problem in a Hamiltonian and attempts to reach its ground state by sufficiently slow interpolation from an easy initial Hamiltonian.","Computation is performed by Hamiltonian evolution whose success depends on spectral gaps and the adiabatic theorem.",["quantum computation","adiabatic theorem","Hamiltonian","optimization"],[],"computation framework"),
    T("measurement-based-qc","Measurement-based quantum computation",2001,"2000–2014","Quantum information & open systems","established framework","Measurement-based quantum computation processes information through adaptive local measurements on a highly entangled resource state.","A pre-entangled cluster or graph state supplies the resource while measurement choices and feed-forward implement the computation.",["MBQC","cluster state","measurement","quantum computation"],["one-way quantum computer"],"computation framework"),
    T("topological-qc","Topological quantum computation",2003,"2000–2014","Quantum information & open systems","active research","Topological quantum computation encodes and processes quantum information in nonlocal degrees of freedom associated with anyons or related topological structures.","Braiding and fusion operations act on a protected computational state space determined by topological charge.",["anyons","braiding","topological order","quantum computation"],[],"computation framework"),
    T("higher-spin-gravity","Higher-spin gravity",2004,"2000–2014","Quantum gravity & spacetime","active research","Higher-spin gravity studies interacting gauge theories containing massless fields of spin greater than two, often in anti-de Sitter spacetime.","An enlarged gauge structure couples an infinite tower of higher-spin fields and provides a distinctive route to quantum-gravity and holographic models.",["higher spin","Vasiliev","AdS","gauge theory"],[],"quantum-gravity approach"),
    T("mera","MERA / entanglement-renormalization framework",2007,"2000–2014","Quantum information & open systems","established framework","Entanglement renormalization uses unitary disentanglers before coarse-graining, leading to the multiscale entanglement renormalization ansatz.","A layered tensor network organizes entanglement by length scale and can efficiently represent scale-invariant many-body states.",["MERA","entanglement renormalization","tensor networks","RG"],[],"mathematical framework"),
    T("topos-contextuality-sheaf","Sheaf-theoretic contextuality",2011,"2000–2014","Mathematical structures","active research","The sheaf-theoretic framework gives a unified mathematical account of contextuality and nonlocality using the existence or obstruction of global sections.","Compatible local measurement data form a presheaf; contextuality appears when they cannot be glued into a global assignment.",["sheaf theory","contextuality","nonlocality","global sections"],[],"mathematical framework"),
    T("zx-calculus","ZX calculus",2011,"2000–2014","Quantum information & open systems","established framework","The ZX calculus is a graphical rewrite language for quantum states, circuits and complementary observables based on interacting algebraic generators.","Quantum computations can be transformed and proved equivalent by diagrammatic rewrite rules rather than matrix calculation alone.",["ZX calculus","diagrammatic reasoning","categorical QM","quantum circuits"],[],"diagrammatic framework"),
    T("causal-fermion-systems","Causal fermion systems",2011,"2000–2014","Quantum gravity & spacetime","active research","Causal fermion systems encode spacetime, causal relations and physical fields through a measure on a space of linear operators governed by a causal action principle.","Continuum spacetime and geometry are intended to emerge from an operator-theoretic variational structure rather than being fundamental input.",["causal fermion systems","emergent spacetime","causal action","operators"],[],"quantum-spacetime framework"),
    T("many-interacting-worlds","Many interacting worlds",2014,"2000–2014","Beyond standard quantum theory","speculative","The many-interacting-worlds approach models quantum phenomena using a large ensemble of classical configuration-space worlds coupled by an inter-world interaction.","The wavefunction is intended to emerge approximately from the collective dynamics of many deterministic worlds rather than being fundamental.",["MIW","emergent quantum mechanics","many worlds","deterministic"],[],"alternative theory"),
    T("string-field-theory","String field theory",1986,"1980–1999","Quantum gravity & spacetime","active research","String field theory promotes strings to field-like degrees of freedom whose interactions are encoded by an action on the space of string configurations.","Splitting and joining of strings are described by interaction vertices in a second-quantized string framework.",["string field theory","BRST","strings","second quantization"],[],"quantum-gravity framework"),
    T("bfss-matrix","BFSS Matrix theory",1997,"1980–1999","Quantum gravity & spacetime","active research","BFSS Matrix theory conjectures that a large-N supersymmetric matrix quantum mechanics gives a nonperturbative formulation of M-theory in an appropriate frame.","D0-brane matrix degrees of freedom are proposed to encode the full dynamics of uncompactified eleven-dimensional M-theory.",["BFSS","M-theory","matrix model","D0 branes"],["Matrix theory"],"quantum-gravity approach"),
    T("ikkt-matrix","IKKT / IIB matrix model",1997,"1980–1999","Quantum gravity & spacetime","active research","The IKKT model proposes a zero-dimensional large-N matrix model as a constructive formulation related to type IIB superstring theory.","Ten-dimensional matrix degrees of freedom and supersymmetry replace an a priori spacetime background in the proposed nonperturbative description.",["IKKT","IIB matrix model","matrix model","emergent spacetime"],[],"quantum-gravity approach"),
    T("modal-quantum-theory","Modal quantum theory",2010,"2000–2014","Beyond standard quantum theory","toy model","Modal quantum theory is a finite-field analogue of quantum mechanics that keeps linear state-space structure but replaces numerical probabilities with possibility and impossibility.","States are vectors over finite fields and measurement predictions are modal rather than probabilistic, while entanglement and no-cloning analogues remain possible.",["finite field","modal","toy theory","post-quantum"],[],"toy theory")
,
    T("background-field-method","Background-field method",1967,"1960–1979","Formulations","established framework","The background-field method quantizes gauge theories by separating fields into background and quantum parts while preserving explicit gauge covariance with respect to the background.","Gauge fixing is applied to quantum fluctuations around a background field so that the effective action retains a useful background gauge invariance.",["background field","gauge theory","effective action","quantization"],[],"quantization framework"),
    T("chiral-perturbation-theory","Chiral perturbation theory",1984,"1980–1999","Quantum field theory","established framework","Chiral perturbation theory is the low-energy effective field theory of QCD built from the approximate chiral symmetry of light quarks and its spontaneous breaking.","Hadronic amplitudes are organized in a controlled expansion in momenta and light-quark masses using the most general chiral-symmetric effective Lagrangian.",["ChPT","QCD","effective field theory","chiral symmetry"],[],"effective field theory"),
    T("heavy-quark-effective-theory","Heavy-quark effective theory",1989,"1980–1999","Quantum field theory","established framework","HQET is an effective theory for hadrons containing quarks much heavier than the QCD scale.","The dynamics are expanded in inverse powers of the heavy-quark mass, exposing heavy-quark spin and flavor symmetries.",["HQET","QCD","heavy quarks","effective field theory"],[],"effective field theory"),
    T("standard-model-eft","Standard Model effective field theory",2010,"2000–2014","Quantum field theory","active research","SMEFT extends the Standard Model Lagrangian by higher-dimensional operators built from Standard Model fields and respecting its gauge symmetries.","Possible heavy new physics is parameterized systematically by operator coefficients suppressed by powers of a high energy scale.",["SMEFT","Standard Model","effective field theory","dimension six"],[],"effective field theory"),
    T("soft-collinear-effective-theory","Soft-collinear effective theory",2001,"2000–2014","Quantum field theory","established framework","SCET is an effective field theory for processes containing energetic collinear particles interacting with soft degrees of freedom.","Separate momentum modes are factorized and matched so large scale ratios and Sudakov logarithms can be treated systematically.",["SCET","QCD","factorization","effective field theory"],[],"effective field theory"),
    T("noncommutative-qft","Noncommutative quantum field theory",1999,"1980–1999","Quantum field theory","active research","Noncommutative QFT studies field theories defined on spaces whose coordinate functions or operators fail to commute.","Ordinary pointwise multiplication is replaced by a noncommutative product, modifying locality, ultraviolet behavior and gauge structure.",["noncommutative spacetime","QFT","star product","string theory"],[],"research framework"),
    T("supersymmetric-localization","Supersymmetric localization",2012,"2000–2014","Quantum field theory","established framework","Supersymmetric localization reduces certain supersymmetric quantum-field-theory path integrals to lower-dimensional or finite-dimensional exact calculations.","A supersymmetry-exact deformation leaves protected observables invariant while localizing the functional integral onto special field configurations.",["localization","supersymmetry","exact results","path integral"],[],"nonperturbative framework"),
    T("peps","Projected entangled-pair states",2004,"2000–2014","Quantum information & open systems","established framework","PEPS generalize matrix-product states to two and higher spatial dimensions as tensor-network representations of quantum many-body states.","Local tensors with contracted virtual indices encode entanglement and provide variational descriptions of higher-dimensional many-body systems.",["PEPS","tensor networks","many-body","entanglement"],["projected entangled-pair states"],"mathematical framework"),
    T("continuous-quantum-measurement","Continuous quantum measurement",2006,"2000–2014","Quantum information & open systems","established framework","Continuous-measurement theory describes the gradual acquisition of information from a quantum system under ongoing weak monitoring.","Conditioned quantum states follow stochastic master equations combining measurement backaction, information gain and ordinary dynamics.",["continuous measurement","stochastic master equation","measurement backaction","open systems"],[],"measurement framework"),
    T("device-independent-qi","Device-independent quantum information",2007,"2000–2014","Quantum information & open systems","active research","Device-independent quantum information certifies tasks from observed input-output statistics without requiring a detailed trusted model of the internal devices.","Bell-type nonlocal correlations provide operational constraints that can certify randomness, security or entanglement from behavior alone.",["device independent","Bell nonlocality","cryptography","certification"],[],"operational framework"),
    T("quantum-filtering","Quantum filtering",1992,"1980–1999","Quantum information & open systems","established framework","Quantum filtering gives stochastic equations for estimating a quantum system's conditional state from a continuous measurement record.","Noncommutative conditional expectations update the system state in real time as measurement outcomes arrive.",["quantum filtering","Belavkin","continuous measurement","stochastic calculus"],[],"dynamical framework"),
    T("gravity-effective-field-theory","Gravity as an effective field theory",1994,"1980–1999","Quantum gravity & spacetime","established effective framework","The effective-field-theory treatment of general relativity quantizes low-energy gravitational fluctuations without requiring a complete ultraviolet theory of quantum gravity.","Unknown short-distance physics is encoded in higher-curvature operators while low-energy quantum corrections from massless fields remain predictive.",["gravity EFT","quantum gravity","low energy","effective field theory"],[],"quantum-gravity framework"),
    T("twistor-string","Twistor string theory",2004,"2000–2014","Quantum gravity & spacetime","active research","Twistor-string theory connects gauge-theory scattering amplitudes with string-like models formulated on twistor space.","Perturbative amplitudes, especially in supersymmetric gauge theory, are reorganized in terms of holomorphic geometric structures in twistor space.",["twistor string","twistor theory","scattering amplitudes","string theory"],[],"research program"),
    T("kappa-poincare","κ-Poincaré / κ-Minkowski framework",1994,"1980–1999","Quantum gravity & spacetime","active research","κ-Poincaré deforms Poincaré symmetry through a quantum-group structure and acts naturally on a related noncommutative κ-Minkowski spacetime.","Planck-scale kinematics can be encoded through deformed momentum composition, coproducts and noncommuting spacetime coordinates.",["kappa Poincare","kappa Minkowski","quantum group","noncommutative spacetime"],[],"quantum-spacetime framework"),
    T("ekpyrotic-cosmology","Ekpyrotic cosmology",2001,"2000–2014","Quantum cosmology","active research","Ekpyrotic cosmology proposes that a hot big-bang phase can emerge after a slowly contracting phase, originally motivated by brane dynamics.","Slow contraction with a stiff effective equation of state can smooth and flatten the universe before a transition into expansion.",["ekpyrotic","brane cosmology","contraction","early universe"],[],"cosmological framework"),
    T("cyclic-cosmology","Cyclic cosmology",2002,"2000–2014","Quantum cosmology","speculative","Modern cyclic cosmologies propose repeated cosmic epochs involving expansion and contraction rather than a single beginning.","A long sequence of cycles is arranged so each new hot phase follows a preceding contracting phase, with model-dependent mechanisms controlling the bounce or transition.",["cyclic universe","ekpyrotic","bounce","cosmology"],[],"cosmological framework"),
    T("parastatistics","Parastatistics",1953,"1940–1959","Beyond standard quantum theory","established framework","Parastatistics generalizes ordinary Bose and Fermi field quantization by allowing higher-order exchange-statistics representations.","Creation and annihilation operators obey generalized trilinear relations that contain ordinary bosonic and fermionic statistics as special cases.",["parastatistics","parafermions","parabosons","quantum statistics"],[],"generalized statistics framework"),
    T("generalized-exclusion-statistics","Generalized exclusion statistics",1991,"1980–1999","Beyond standard quantum theory","established framework","Haldane exclusion statistics generalizes the Pauli principle by allowing the available one-particle state-space dimension to change fractionally as particles are added.","Statistical interactions are characterized by how particle number changes the dimension of accessible state space rather than only by exchange phases.",["Haldane statistics","exclusion statistics","fractional statistics","many-body"],[],"generalized statistics framework"),
    T("doebner-goldin","Doebner–Goldin nonlinear quantum mechanics",1992,"1980–1999","Beyond standard quantum theory","speculative","Doebner–Goldin equations form a family of nonlinear Schrödinger dynamics motivated by representations of current algebras and diffusion-like terms.","The usual Schrödinger equation is extended by nonlinear and dissipative terms related through nonlinear gauge transformations.",["Doebner-Goldin","nonlinear Schrödinger","nonlinear gauge","diffusion"],[],"alternative theory")
