    T("collision-models","Quantum collision models / repeated interactions",2002,"2000–2014","Quantum information & open systems","active research","Quantum collision models represent an environment as a stream of ancillary subsystems that interact with the system one after another.","Repeated unitary system–ancilla interactions provide a discrete microscopic construction of open-system dynamics, master equations, memory effects and thermodynamic exchanges.",["collision models","repeated interactions","open systems","ancillas"],[],"dynamical framework"),
    T("quantum-supermaps","Quantum supermaps",2008,"2000–2014","Quantum information & open systems","established framework","Quantum supermaps are higher-order quantum transformations that take quantum operations as inputs and return quantum operations as outputs.","Completely positive transformations of channels can themselves be represented and physically realized as higher-order quantum circuits.",["quantum supermaps","higher-order maps","channels","quantum networks"],[],"process framework"),
    T("causal-boxes","Causal boxes",2015,"2015–present","Quantum information & open systems","active research","Causal boxes model quantum information-processing systems whose messages can have nontrivial and even superposed timing or causal structure while remaining closed under composition.","Systems are specified by families of quantum maps over spacetime message positions, allowing composable analysis of indefinite or relativistic causal scenarios.",["causal boxes","composition","indefinite causal structure","cryptography"],[],"process framework"),
    T("pseudo-density-matrix","Pseudo-density-matrix framework",2015,"2015–present","Quantum information & open systems","active research","The pseudo-density-matrix framework extends density-matrix-like descriptions across both spatially and temporally separated measurement events.","Multi-time correlations are encoded in an operator that need not remain positive, enabling operational distinction between spatial and temporal correlations.",["pseudo-density matrix","temporal correlations","causality","multi-time"],[],"process framework"),
    T("euclidean-dynamical-triangulations","Euclidean dynamical triangulations",1992,"1980–1999","Quantum gravity & spacetime","active research","Euclidean dynamical triangulations approximate the gravitational path integral by summing over piecewise-flat Euclidean simplicial manifolds.","Fixed-edge-length triangulations supply a discrete ensemble of geometries whose statistical phases are studied for possible continuum gravitational behavior.",["EDT","dynamical triangulations","simplicial gravity","path integral"],[],"quantum-gravity approach"),
    T("twisted-geometries","Twisted geometries",2010,"2000–2014","Quantum gravity & spacetime","active research","Twisted geometries provide a geometric parametrization of the fixed-graph phase space used in loop quantum gravity.","Neighboring polyhedra can assign compatible areas but mismatched shapes to shared faces, yielding discrete geometries that generalize Regge geometries.",["twisted geometries","LQG","spin networks","discrete geometry"],[],"quantum-geometry framework"),
    T("master-constraint-program","Master Constraint Programme",2006,"2000–2014","Quantum gravity & spacetime","active research","The Master Constraint Programme reformulates the many Hamiltonian constraints of canonical loop quantum gravity into a single positive master constraint.","Combining constraints into one operator is intended to simplify the constraint algebra, physical-state space and construction of Dirac observables.",["master constraint","LQG","Hamiltonian constraint","Dirac observables"],[],"quantum-gravity program"),
    T("group-field-cosmology","Group-field cosmology",2013,"2000–2014","Quantum cosmology","active research","Group-field cosmology derives effective homogeneous cosmological dynamics from collective condensate states of group-field-theory quanta.","Many microscopic quantum-geometry degrees of freedom are treated as a condensate whose effective dynamics can produce modified Friedmann equations.",["group field cosmology","GFT condensate","emergent cosmology","quantum geometry"],[],"cosmological framework"),
    T("spin-foam-cosmology","Spin-foam cosmology",2010,"2000–2014","Quantum cosmology","active research","Spin-foam cosmology applies spin-foam transition amplitudes to highly symmetric or coarse cosmological boundary states.","Quantum amplitudes for homogeneous and isotropic geometries are extracted from spin-foam dynamics and compared with Friedmann-like evolution.",["spin foam cosmology","spin foams","LQG","Friedmann"],[],"cosmological framework"),
    T("pre-big-bang-cosmology","Pre-big-bang string cosmology",1993,"1980–1999","Quantum cosmology","active research","Pre-big-bang string cosmology uses string dualities and the dilaton to construct a phase preceding the conventional hot big bang.","Scale-factor duality permits a high-curvature pre-big-bang branch whose evolution is intended to connect to standard expanding cosmology.",["pre-big-bang","string cosmology","duality","dilaton"],[],"cosmological framework")

    T("weyl-quantization","Weyl quantization",1927,"1925–1939","Formulations","established framework","Weyl quantization maps classical phase-space functions to quantum operators using a symmetric Fourier-based prescription.","Classical observables are converted into operators through the Weyl transform, providing a phase-space-centered quantization map closely related to Wigner and deformation formulations.",["Weyl quantization","Weyl transform","phase space","operator ordering"],[],"quantization framework"),
    T("rigged-hilbert-space","Rigged Hilbert space / Gel'fand triplet",1960,"1960–1979","Mathematical structures","established framework","Rigged Hilbert space extends a Hilbert space by a dense test-function space and its dual so generalized eigenvectors can be represented rigorously.","A triplet Φ ⊂ H ⊂ Φ′ gives mathematical meaning to Dirac-style continuous-spectrum eigenkets and distributional states.",["rigged Hilbert space","Gelfand triplet","generalized eigenvectors","Dirac notation"],["Gel'fand triplet"],"mathematical framework"),
    T("noncommutative-probability","Noncommutative / quantum probability",1981,"1980–1999","Mathematical structures","established framework","Quantum probability generalizes classical probability by replacing commutative random-variable algebras with noncommutative operator algebras.","States act as positive normalized functionals on operator algebras, while observables and conditional structures need not commute.",["quantum probability","noncommutative probability","operator algebras","states"],[],"mathematical framework"),
    T("schwinger-dyson","Schwinger–Dyson equations",1951,"1940–1959","Quantum field theory","established framework","Schwinger–Dyson equations are exact functional relations among quantum-field correlation functions derived from the equations of motion or path-integral identities.","The full hierarchy of Green functions obeys coupled integral or differential equations, providing a nonperturbative route when supplemented by truncation or closure schemes.",["Schwinger-Dyson","Green functions","nonperturbative QFT","functional methods"],["Dyson–Schwinger equations"],"nonperturbative framework"),
    T("integrable-qft","Integrable quantum field theory",1979,"1960–1979","Quantum field theory","established framework","Integrable quantum field theories in low dimensions possess infinitely many conserved quantities that strongly constrain scattering and dynamics.","In 1+1 dimensions the scattering matrix can factorize into exact two-particle amplitudes satisfying unitarity, crossing and Yang–Baxter-type consistency.",["integrable QFT","factorized S matrix","1+1 dimensions","exact solutions"],[],"nonperturbative framework"),
    T("nrqed","Nonrelativistic QED (NRQED)",1986,"1980–1999","Quantum field theory","established framework","NRQED is an effective field theory for nonrelativistic charged particles interacting with the quantized electromagnetic field.","Relativistic QED is matched onto an expansion in inverse masses and low velocities, organizing bound-state and atomic corrections systematically.",["NRQED","QED","effective field theory","bound states"],[],"effective field theory"),
    T("nrqcd","Nonrelativistic QCD (NRQCD)",1995,"1980–1999","Quantum field theory","established framework","NRQCD is an effective field theory separating the heavy-quark mass scale from lower momentum and binding scales in heavy-quark systems.","Heavy-quarkonium observables are expanded in short-distance coefficients and nonperturbative matrix elements ordered by powers of the heavy-quark velocity.",["NRQCD","QCD","heavy quarkonium","effective field theory"],[],"effective field theory"),
    T("topological-string","Topological string theory",1992,"1980–1999","Quantum gravity & spacetime","active research","Topological string theories are simplified string models whose amplitudes depend on protected geometric or topological data rather than the full local dynamics of ordinary strings.","Topological sigma models connect string amplitudes to invariants of target-space geometry and to gauge-theory structures such as Chern–Simons theory.",["topological string","string theory","topological sigma model","Chern-Simons"],[],"research program"),
    T("davies-generators","Davies weak-coupling generators",1974,"1960–1979","Quantum information & open systems","established framework","Davies' weak-coupling limit derives Markovian quantum master equations from microscopic system–reservoir dynamics under controlled scaling assumptions.","Long-time weak coupling yields a completely positive quantum dynamical semigroup with transition rates tied to reservoir correlation spectra.",["Davies generator","weak coupling","Markovian master equation","open systems"],[],"dynamical framework"),
    T("contextuality-resource-theory","Resource theory of contextuality",2017,"2015–present","Quantum information & open systems","active research","Resource-theoretic contextuality frameworks quantify contextual behavior relative to specified noncontextual free states and operations.","Contextuality is treated as an operational resource with monotones and conversion rules, connecting quantum foundations to advantages in information-processing tasks.",["contextuality","resource theory","generalized contextuality","quantum advantage"],[],"resource framework")

    T("algebraic-quantum-gravity","Algebraic Quantum Gravity (AQG)",2006,"2000–2014","Quantum gravity & spacetime","active research","Algebraic Quantum Gravity is a graph-algebraic approach to canonical quantum gravity inspired by loop quantum gravity but formulated on an abstract algebraic graph.","The kinematical operator algebra and a Master Constraint are defined without fundamental manifold topology, while semiclassical states are used to recover continuum geometry and low-energy fields.",["AQG","algebraic graph","Master Constraint","canonical quantum gravity"],[],"quantum-gravity approach"),
    T("tensorial-group-field-theory","Tensorial group field theory",2013,"2000–2014","Quantum gravity & spacetime","active research","Tensorial group field theories combine group-field-theory degrees of freedom with tensor-model combinatorics and renormalization techniques.","Fields on group manifolds carry tensor-invariant interactions whose Feynman diagrams generate discrete quantum geometries, allowing large-N and renormalization methods to be applied to GFT.",["tensorial GFT","group field theory","tensor models","renormalization"],[],"quantum-gravity approach"),
    T("lorentzian-quantum-cosmology","Lorentzian / Picard–Lefschetz quantum cosmology",2017,"2015–present","Quantum cosmology","active research","Lorentzian quantum cosmology evaluates gravitational path integrals directly in Lorentzian signature using complex-contour and Picard–Lefschetz methods.","Oscillatory path integrals are deformed onto steepest-descent contours to determine contributing saddle geometries without assuming a Euclidean rotation.",["Lorentzian path integral","Picard-Lefschetz","quantum cosmology","no-boundary"],[],"cosmological framework"),
    T("primitive-ontology","Primitive-ontology program",2008,"2000–2014","Foundations & interpretations","active research","Primitive-ontology approaches require a quantum theory to specify matter distributed in ordinary space or spacetime in addition to its wavefunction or dynamical law.","Particles, matter-density fields or spacetime flashes supply the primitive variables from which macroscopic records and empirical predictions are read.",["primitive ontology","Bohmian mechanics","GRW","ontology"],[],"foundational framework"),
    T("grwm","GRW matter-density theory (GRWm)",2008,"2000–2014","Foundations & interpretations","alternative theory","GRWm combines GRW spontaneous-collapse dynamics with a continuous matter-density field in physical space as the theory's primitive ontology.","The wavefunction undergoes GRW collapses while its mass-density functional specifies how matter is distributed in three-dimensional space.",["GRWm","matter density","collapse","primitive ontology"],[],"alternative theory"),
    T("grwf","GRW flash theory (GRWf)",2008,"2000–2014","Foundations & interpretations","alternative theory","GRWf combines GRW collapse dynamics with a sparse ontology of discrete spacetime events called flashes.","Each collapse is associated with a spacetime flash, and the complete pattern of flashes constitutes the material history of the theory.",["GRWf","flash ontology","collapse","primitive ontology"],[],"alternative theory"),
    T("qmupl","QMUPL collapse model",2003,"2000–2014","Foundations & interpretations","alternative theory","QMUPL is a continuous stochastic wavefunction-collapse model often used as a mathematically simpler relative of GRW and CSL.","Position-localizing stochastic terms continuously drive state reduction while preserving approximately standard microscopic quantum behavior.",["QMUPL","collapse","stochastic dynamics","localization"],[],"alternative theory")

    T("history-projection-operator","History Projection Operator (HPO) formalism",1994,"1980–1999","Mathematical structures","active research","The HPO formalism represents propositions about multi-time quantum histories as genuine projection operators on a history Hilbert space.","Tensor products of single-time projectors define homogeneous history propositions, extending quantum logic to temporal propositions and continuous-time histories.",["HPO","histories","temporal quantum logic","projection operators"],["History Projection Operator formalism"],"formal framework"),
    T("coevent-interpretation","Coevent / anhomomorphic-logic interpretation",2007,"2000–2014","Foundations & interpretations","interpretation","The coevent interpretation of quantum measure theory replaces classical Boolean truth assignments with more general anhomomorphic valuations on histories.","A coevent assigns truth values to events while relaxing classical homomorphism requirements, aiming to define an observer-independent realized history compatible with quantum interference.",["coevents","anhomomorphic logic","quantum measure","histories"],[],"interpretation"),
    T("decoherent-histories-cosmology","Decoherent-histories quantum cosmology",1990,"1980–1999","Quantum cosmology","active research","Decoherent-histories quantum cosmology applies generalized histories-based quantum mechanics to the universe as a closed quantum system.","Probabilities are assigned to coarse-grained cosmological histories when interference between alternatives is sufficiently suppressed, avoiding reliance on external measurements or observers.",["decoherent histories","quantum cosmology","closed systems","coarse graining"],[],"cosmological framework"),
    T("diosi-gravitational-collapse","Diósi gravitational collapse model",1987,"1980–1999","Foundations & interpretations","alternative theory","Diósi proposed a gravity-related modification of quantum dynamics in which superpositions of substantially different mass distributions lose coherence.","A universal master equation introduces mass-density-dependent decoherence tied to Newtonian gravitational structure, providing a concrete precursor to later Diósi–Penrose collapse discussions.",["Diosi","gravitational collapse","mass density","decoherence"],[],"alternative theory"),
    T("energy-driven-collapse","Energy-driven stochastic collapse",1996,"1980–1999","Foundations & interpretations","alternative theory","Energy-driven collapse models modify Schrödinger evolution with nonlinear stochastic terms that reduce superpositions in the energy basis.","The stochastic dynamics are constructed so state-vector diffusion progressively suppresses energy uncertainty while preserving Born-rule probabilities under suitable conditions.",["energy-driven collapse","stochastic reduction","Hughston","nonlinear dynamics"],[],"alternative theory"),
    T("canonical-quantum-gravity","Canonical quantum gravity",1967,"1960–1979","Quantum gravity & spacetime","active research","Canonical quantum gravity quantizes the Hamiltonian formulation of general relativity by promoting geometric phase-space variables and gravitational constraints to quantum operators.","Physical states are selected by quantum constraint equations, including Hamiltonian or Wheeler–DeWitt-type constraints, with loop quantum gravity representing a major later canonical development.",["canonical quantum gravity","Hamiltonian constraint","Wheeler-DeWitt","constraints"],[],"quantum-gravity framework")

    T("operational-reconstruction-qm","Operational / informational reconstructions of quantum theory",2001,"2000–2014","Foundations & interpretations","active research","Operational reconstruction programs seek to derive the mathematical structure of quantum theory from physically motivated axioms about information, composition, probability and reversible transformations.","Rather than assuming complex Hilbert space at the outset, these approaches characterize a broader operational theory space and identify principles—such as continuity or purification—that single out quantum theory.",["operational reconstruction","informational principles","axioms","GPT"],["axiomatic reconstructions of quantum theory"],"foundational framework"),
    T("bell-type-qft","Bell-type quantum field theories",2004,"2000–2014","Beyond standard quantum theory","alternative theory","Bell-type quantum field theories extend Bohmian-style primitive-ontology dynamics to quantum field theories with particle creation and annihilation.","A quantum state guides an equivariant stochastic configuration process, typically with deterministic motion interrupted by jump events whose rates are derived from the interaction Hamiltonian.",["Bell-type QFT","Bohmian QFT","particle creation","jump process"],[],"alternative theory"),
    T("holographic-space-time","Holographic Space-Time (HST)",2011,"2000–2014","Quantum gravity & spacetime","active research","Holographic Space-Time is a quantum-gravity framework in which finite causal diamonds are assigned finite-dimensional quantum systems associated with holographic screens.","Consistency conditions between overlapping observer-dependent Hilbert spaces are used to encode emergent spacetime, particles, black holes and cosmological geometries.",["HST","holography","causal diamonds","emergent spacetime"],["Holographic Space-Time"],"quantum-gravity approach"),
    T("infinite-derivative-gravity","Ghost-free infinite-derivative / nonlocal gravity",2011,"2000–2014","Quantum gravity & spacetime","active research","Infinite-derivative gravity modifies the gravitational action with analytic functions of derivative operators, producing a class of nonlocal higher-curvature theories.","Suitable form factors can improve ultraviolet behavior while avoiding additional propagating ghost poles around selected backgrounds and recovering general relativity at low energies.",["infinite derivative gravity","nonlocal gravity","ghost free","UV gravity"],[],"quantum-gravity approach"),
    T("polymer-quantum-mechanics","Polymer quantum mechanics",2002,"2000–2014","Formulations","active research","Polymer quantum mechanics applies the nonregular representation underlying loop quantum gravity to ordinary finite-dimensional quantum systems as a controlled model of quantum-geometry effects.","Configuration or momentum translation operators are represented discontinuously, so one of the usual canonical operators is absent and dynamics are defined through finite translations or regulated substitutes.",["polymer quantization","loop quantum gravity","nonregular representation","shadow states"],[],"quantization framework"),
    T("causal-set-quantum-dynamics","Causal-set quantum path-sum dynamics",2019,"2015–present","Quantum gravity & spacetime","active research","Quantum causal-set dynamics seeks a genuine quantum dynamics for causal sets using histories, decoherence functionals or discrete gravitational path sums rather than only classical sequential growth.","Quantum measures or action-weighted sums over causal sets provide candidate dynamical frameworks whose continuum behavior and observables remain active research questions.",["causal sets","quantum measure","path sum","discrete quantum gravity"],[],"quantum-gravity approach")

    T("dirac-electron-theory","Dirac relativistic electron theory",1928,"1925–1939","Formulations","established","Dirac's relativistic wave equation describes spin-1/2 particles and predicted antiparticle degrees of freedom before the positron was observed.","A first-order Lorentz-covariant equation uses gamma matrices to combine quantum mechanics with special relativity for fermionic matter.",["Dirac equation","spin-1/2","relativistic quantum mechanics","antimatter"],["Dirac equation"],"formulation"),
    T("quantum-optical-coherence","Glauber quantum optical coherence theory",1963,"1960–1979","Quantum optics & AMO","established framework","Glauber's quantum theory of optical coherence characterizes light through normally ordered field correlation functions and photodetection statistics.","First- and higher-order coherence functions distinguish coherent, thermal and nonclassical radiation using quantum electromagnetic-field operators.",["Glauber","coherence","photodetection","quantum optics"],[],"theory / framework"),
    T("jaynes-cummings","Jaynes–Cummings model",1963,"1960–1979","Quantum optics & AMO","established framework","The Jaynes–Cummings model describes a two-level quantum system resonantly coupled to a single quantized electromagnetic mode under the rotating-wave approximation.","Coherent exchange of one excitation between atom and field produces dressed states, vacuum Rabi oscillations and collapse-revival phenomena.",["Jaynes-Cummings","cavity QED","two-level system","light-matter"],[],"model"),
    T("quantum-rabi-model","Quantum Rabi model",1936,"1925–1939","Quantum optics & AMO","established framework","The quantum Rabi model describes a two-level system coupled to a single quantized bosonic mode without making the rotating-wave approximation.","Counter-rotating interaction terms become important in ultrastrong coupling and distinguish the full Rabi Hamiltonian from the Jaynes–Cummings approximation.",["Rabi model","light-matter","ultrastrong coupling","two-level system"],[],"model"),
    T("bcs-theory","BCS theory of superconductivity",1957,"1940–1959","Quantum many-body & condensed matter","established","BCS theory explains conventional superconductivity through a coherent many-electron state formed by paired fermions near the Fermi surface.","An effective attractive interaction produces Cooper pairing, a superconducting energy gap and spontaneous breaking of electromagnetic U(1) phase symmetry.",["BCS","superconductivity","Cooper pairs","many-body"],[],"theory / framework"),
    T("density-functional-theory","Density functional theory",1964,"1960–1979","Quantum many-body & condensed matter","established framework","Density functional theory recasts the interacting-electron ground-state problem in terms of the spatial particle density rather than the full many-body wavefunction.","Hohenberg–Kohn theorems establish density-based ground-state functionals; Kohn–Sham orbitals provide a practical noninteracting reference system with the same density.",["DFT","Hohenberg-Kohn","Kohn-Sham","electronic structure"],[],"theory / framework"),
    T("hubbard-model","Hubbard model",1963,"1960–1979","Quantum many-body & condensed matter","established framework","The Hubbard model captures competition between quantum hopping and local interactions for particles on a lattice.","A kinetic hopping term competes with an on-site interaction, producing correlated phases including Mott physics, magnetism and model-dependent superconducting regimes.",["Hubbard model","Mott insulator","lattice","strong correlations"],[],"model"),
    T("anderson-localization","Anderson localization",1958,"1940–1959","Quantum many-body & condensed matter","established framework","Anderson localization describes suppression of wave transport by coherent multiple scattering in a disordered quantum medium.","Sufficient disorder can produce spatially localized stationary states and vanishing diffusion even without conventional trapping.",["Anderson localization","disorder","interference","transport"],[],"theory / framework"),
    T("integer-quantum-hall","Integer quantum Hall effect",1980,"1980–1999","Quantum many-body & condensed matter","established","The integer quantum Hall effect exhibits precisely quantized transverse conductance for two-dimensional electrons in strong magnetic fields.","Landau-level filling and topological Chern invariants underlie plateaus with Hall conductance in integer multiples of e²/h.",["IQHE","Chern number","Landau levels","topological phase"],[],"theory / framework"),
    T("fractional-quantum-hall","Fractional quantum Hall / Laughlin theory",1982,"1980–1999","Quantum many-body & condensed matter","established","Fractional quantum Hall states arise from strongly correlated two-dimensional electrons and support fractionally charged quasiparticles and topological order.","Laughlin's correlated many-body wavefunction captures prominent fractional filling states and implies anyonic quasiparticle excitations.",["FQHE","Laughlin","fractional charge","topological order"],[],"theory / framework"),
    T("bogoliubov-bose-gas","Bogoliubov theory of weakly interacting Bose gases",1947,"1940–1959","Quantum many-body & condensed matter","established framework","Bogoliubov theory treats a weakly interacting Bose condensate by expanding around a macroscopically occupied mode and diagonalizing quadratic fluctuations.","A canonical transformation yields quasiparticle excitations with a phonon-like low-momentum spectrum and quantum depletion of the condensate.",["Bogoliubov","Bose gas","quasiparticles","BEC"],[],"many-body framework"),
    T("gross-pitaevskii","Gross–Pitaevskii mean-field theory",1961,"1960–1979","Quantum many-body & condensed matter","established framework","Gross–Pitaevskii theory describes a dilute Bose–Einstein condensate using a nonlinear macroscopic wavefunction.","A nonlinear Schrödinger equation with contact interaction captures condensate density, collective dynamics, vortices and weakly interacting mean-field behavior.",["Gross-Pitaevskii","BEC","nonlinear Schrödinger","mean field"],[],"many-body framework"),
    T("kondo-model","Kondo model / Kondo effect",1964,"1960–1979","Quantum many-body & condensed matter","established framework","The Kondo model describes antiferromagnetic exchange between a localized magnetic impurity and itinerant conduction electrons.","Many-body screening of the impurity spin generates a low-energy Kondo scale and characteristic logarithmic transport behavior.",["Kondo","magnetic impurity","screening","strong correlations"],[],"model"),
    T("haldane-model","Haldane Chern-insulator model",1988,"1980–1999","Quantum many-body & condensed matter","established framework","The Haldane model demonstrates a quantized Hall phase on a lattice with zero net magnetic flux through the unit cell.","Complex next-nearest-neighbor hopping breaks time-reversal symmetry and produces bands with nonzero Chern number without ordinary Landau levels.",["Haldane model","Chern insulator","topological band theory","quantum Hall"],[],"model"),
    T("toric-code","Toric-code model",1997,"1980–1999","Quantum many-body & condensed matter","established framework","Kitaev's toric code is an exactly solvable lattice model exhibiting intrinsic topological order and anyonic excitations.","Commuting star and plaquette operators generate a topologically degenerate ground space whose excitations have nontrivial braiding statistics and quantum-error-correcting structure.",["toric code","topological order","anyons","quantum error correction"],[],"model")

    T("quantum-error-correction","Quantum error-correction theory",1996,"1980–1999","Quantum information & open systems","established framework","Quantum error correction protects encoded quantum information against a specified set of errors by embedding logical states into a larger Hilbert space and recovering them without directly measuring the encoded quantum amplitudes.","Correctable error sets satisfy algebraic conditions on the code subspace, enabling syndrome extraction and recovery while preserving logical coherence.",["quantum error correction","Knill-Laflamme","codes","fault tolerance"],["QEC"],"theory / framework"),
    T("stabilizer-formalism","Stabilizer formalism",1997,"1980–1999","Quantum information & open systems","established framework","The stabilizer formalism describes an important class of quantum states and codes through commuting subgroups of the Pauli group.","A stabilizer state or code is the simultaneous +1 eigenspace of commuting Pauli operators, making Clifford circuits and many error-correcting codes efficiently tractable.",["stabilizer","Pauli group","Clifford","quantum codes"],[],"formal framework"),
    T("surface-code","Surface-code quantum error correction",2002,"2000–2014","Quantum information & open systems","active research","Surface codes encode logical qubits in local stabilizer checks arranged on a two-dimensional lattice and are a leading architecture for fault-tolerant quantum computing.","Logical information is stored nonlocally while repeated local syndrome measurements detect error chains whose homology determines logical failure.",["surface code","topological code","fault tolerance","stabilizer"],[],"code framework"),
    T("continuous-variable-qi","Continuous-variable quantum information",1998,"1980–1999","Quantum information & open systems","established framework","Continuous-variable quantum information encodes and processes quantum states in bosonic quadratures rather than finite-dimensional qubits.","Gaussian states, symplectic transformations, squeezing and homodyne measurements form a central toolbox for optical quantum communication and computation.",["continuous variables","Gaussian states","quadratures","bosonic modes"],["CV quantum information"],"theory / framework"),
    T("gkp-code","Gottesman–Kitaev–Preskill bosonic code",2001,"2000–2014","Quantum information & open systems","active research","The GKP code embeds a finite-dimensional logical qubit into the continuous phase space of a harmonic oscillator using a periodic grid of position and momentum peaks.","Displacement errors smaller than half the lattice spacing can be diagnosed through modular quadrature measurements and corrected.",["GKP","bosonic code","continuous variables","quantum error correction"],[],"code framework"),
    T("quantum-metrology","Quantum metrology",2004,"2000–2014","Quantum information & open systems","established framework","Quantum metrology studies estimation of physical parameters using quantum states, measurements and entanglement to improve precision beyond classical strategies under specified resources.","Quantum Fisher information and Cramér–Rao bounds quantify attainable sensitivity, while entanglement, squeezing and adaptive measurements can enhance performance.",["quantum metrology","Fisher information","sensing","precision"],[],"operational framework"),
    T("spin-squeezing","Spin squeezing",1992,"1980–1999","Quantum information & open systems","established framework","Spin squeezing redistributes collective-spin quantum fluctuations so that one transverse component has reduced variance at the cost of increased conjugate noise.","Appropriate spin-squeezed states can improve Ramsey-type phase estimation and provide witnesses of useful multipartite entanglement.",["spin squeezing","collective spin","metrology","entanglement"],[],"resource framework")

    T("hartree-fock","Hartree–Fock method",1930,"1925–1939","Quantum chemistry & electronic structure","established framework","Hartree–Fock approximates an interacting fermionic many-body state by a single antisymmetrized Slater determinant and determines its orbitals self-consistently.","Exchange arises exactly within the single-determinant ansatz while dynamical electron correlation beyond that ansatz is omitted.",["Hartree-Fock","Slater determinant","exchange","self-consistent field"],["HF"],"many-body framework"),
    T("configuration-interaction","Configuration-interaction method",1950,"1940–1959","Quantum chemistry & electronic structure","established framework","Configuration interaction expands a many-electron wavefunction as a linear combination of Slater determinants or configuration state functions built from a chosen orbital basis.","Full CI is exact within a finite one-particle basis but its determinant space grows combinatorially; truncated CI provides systematic but non-size-extensive approximations.",["configuration interaction","determinants","electronic structure","correlation"],["CI"],"many-body framework"),
    T("moller-plesset","Møller–Plesset perturbation theory",1934,"1925–1939","Quantum chemistry & electronic structure","established framework","Møller–Plesset theory treats electron correlation as perturbative corrections around a Hartree–Fock reference.","Orders such as MP2, MP3 and MP4 arise by partitioning the electronic Hamiltonian into the Fock operator plus a residual interaction.",["Moller-Plesset","MP2","perturbation theory","correlation"],["MP perturbation theory"],"many-body framework"),
    T("coupled-cluster","Coupled-cluster theory",1958,"1940–1959","Quantum chemistry & electronic structure","established framework","Coupled-cluster theory parametrizes a correlated many-electron state with an exponential excitation operator acting on a reference determinant.","The exponential ansatz produces size-extensive approximations such as CCSD and CCSD(T) while summing selected perturbative contributions to infinite order.",["coupled cluster","CCSD","CCSD(T)","electronic correlation"],["CC theory"],"many-body framework"),
    T("time-dependent-dft","Time-dependent density-functional theory",1984,"1980–1999","Quantum chemistry & electronic structure","established framework","Time-dependent density-functional theory extends density-based electronic-structure theory to time-dependent external potentials and excited-state response.","The Runge–Gross theorem establishes the central time-dependent density–potential mapping, while practical calculations often use time-dependent Kohn–Sham equations.",["TDDFT","Runge-Gross","excited states","response"],[],"theory / framework"),
    T("gw-approximation","GW approximation",1965,"1960–1979","Quantum chemistry & electronic structure","established framework","The GW approximation estimates the electronic self-energy as a product of a one-particle Green function and a dynamically screened Coulomb interaction.","It is widely used to improve quasiparticle excitation energies beyond static mean-field electronic-structure methods.",["GW","self energy","screened interaction","quasiparticles"],[],"many-body framework"),
    T("bethe-salpeter","Bethe–Salpeter equation for two-particle excitations",1951,"1940–1959","Quantum chemistry & electronic structure","established framework","The Bethe–Salpeter equation is an integral equation for correlated two-particle amplitudes and is widely used with GW-type inputs for neutral excitations and optical spectra.","A two-particle kernel couples electron–hole configurations and captures excitonic effects beyond independent-quasiparticle descriptions.",["Bethe-Salpeter","BSE","excitons","two-particle Green function"],[],"many-body framework"),
    T("dmrg","Density-matrix renormalization group",1992,"1980–1999","Quantum many-body & condensed matter","established framework","DMRG is a variational renormalization algorithm that retains the most important states of a subsystem according to reduced-density-matrix eigenvalues.","Its modern tensor-network interpretation identifies DMRG as an optimization method over matrix-product states, particularly powerful in one dimension.",["DMRG","matrix product states","renormalization","strong correlations"],[],"many-body framework"),
    T("dmft","Dynamical mean-field theory",1992,"1980–1999","Quantum many-body & condensed matter","established framework","Dynamical mean-field theory maps a lattice many-body problem onto a self-consistent quantum impurity model with a frequency-dependent local environment.","The method becomes exact in an infinite-coordination limit and captures local dynamical correlations central to Mott physics.",["DMFT","Hubbard model","impurity model","strong correlations"],[],"many-body framework"),
    T("quantum-monte-carlo","Quantum Monte Carlo",1980,"1980–1999","Quantum many-body & condensed matter","established framework","Quantum Monte Carlo denotes stochastic methods that evaluate quantum expectation values, path integrals or projector dynamics by sampling high-dimensional probability distributions.","Major families include variational, diffusion, path-integral and auxiliary-field Monte Carlo, with fermionic sign problems limiting many applications.",["QMC","Monte Carlo","path integral","many-body"],[],"computational framework")
,
    T("hidden-measurements","Hidden-measurements approach",1986,"1980–1999","Foundations & interpretations","active research","The hidden-measurements approach explains quantum probabilities through lack of knowledge about which measurement interaction is actualized, rather than only through ignorance of a pre-existing system state.","A measurement is modeled as a family of possible interactions; averaging over inaccessible interaction details can generate non-Kolmogorovian quantum-like probabilities.",["hidden measurements","measurement interaction","Aerts","quantum probability"],[],"foundational framework"),
    T("operational-quantum-logic","Operational quantum logic",2000,"2000–2014","Mathematical structures","active research","Operational quantum logic develops quantum-logical structures from experimentally meaningful preparations, tests, effects, and probabilistic state spaces rather than starting only from the Hilbert-space projection lattice.","Convex operational models, effect algebras, ordered vector spaces, and related structures connect quantum logic to information-processing and generalized probabilistic frameworks.",["operational quantum logic","effect algebra","convexity","quantum foundations"],[],"formal framework"),
    T("polymer-quantum-cosmology","Polymer quantum cosmology",2019,"2015–present","Quantum cosmology","active research","Polymer quantum cosmology applies polymer quantization directly to reduced cosmological phase spaces and studies how the resulting discrete/holonomy structure modifies early-universe dynamics.","Polymerized canonical variables replace ordinary momentum dependence with bounded holonomy-like functions, producing modified effective constraints and Friedmann dynamics outside a single fixed LQC quantization prescription.",["polymer cosmology","polymer quantization","holonomy","quantum cosmology"],[],"cosmological framework"),

    T("gleason-theorem","Gleason's theorem",1957,"1940–1959","Foundations & interpretations","established theorem","Gleason's theorem characterizes probability measures on Hilbert-space projectors and under standard dimensional assumptions yields the density-operator/Born-rule form.","For Hilbert spaces of dimension at least three, noncontextual probability measures on projectors are represented by positive trace-one operators.",["Born rule","probability","Hilbert space","foundations"],[],"theorem"),
    T("ghz-nonlocality","GHZ nonlocality theorem",1990,"1980–1999","Foundations & interpretations","established theorem","The Greenberger–Horne–Zeilinger construction gives an inequality-free multipartite conflict between quantum predictions and local predetermined values.","Multipartite entangled states permit perfect-correlation predictions that cannot be assigned consistently by local hidden variables.",["GHZ","Bell","nonlocality","entanglement"],["Greenberger–Horne–Zeilinger argument"],"theorem"),
    T("frauchiger-renner","Frauchiger–Renner no-go argument",2018,"2015–present","Foundations & interpretations","active foundational result","Frauchiger and Renner constructed an extended Wigner's-friend scenario in which a stated set of assumptions about universal quantum theory, consistency and single outcomes cannot all be maintained together.","Nested quantum observers generate incompatible inferences when the paper's assumptions Q, C and S are imposed simultaneously; the interpretation of the result remains debated.",["Wigner's friend","measurement problem","no-go theorem","observers"],[],"theorem"),
    T("quantum-instruments","Quantum instruments and generalized measurement",1970,"1960–1979","Formulations","established framework","Quantum-instrument theory unifies measurement outcome probabilities with the state transformations conditioned on those outcomes.","A measurement is represented by a family of completely positive operations whose traces give outcome probabilities and whose normalized outputs give posterior states.",["measurement","instruments","POVM","operations"],["operational quantum measurement theory"],"formulation"),
    T("dhr-superselection","DHR superselection-sector theory",1971,"1960–1979","Quantum field theory","established framework","Doplicher–Haag–Roberts theory classifies localized superselection sectors of algebraic quantum field theory and relates charge structure to internal symmetries.","Localized representations of the observable algebra encode charge sectors whose composition and statistics reconstruct gauge structure.",["AQFT","superselection","charges","gauge symmetry"],["Doplicher–Haag–Roberts theory"],"axiomatic framework"),
    T("constructor-theory","Constructor theory",2015,"2015–present","Foundations & interpretations","active research","Constructor theory proposes expressing fundamental laws through which physical transformations are possible, impossible, or arbitrarily accurately realizable rather than only through trajectories of states.","Counterfactual statements about tasks and constructors are treated as fundamental law-like content, with information principles formulated inside that task-based framework.",["constructor theory","information","counterfactuals","foundations"],[],"research program"),
    T("qft-curved-spacetime","Quantum field theory in curved spacetime",1969,"1960–1979","Quantum field theory","established framework","Quantum field theory in curved spacetime quantizes matter fields on a prescribed classical curved geometry and provides the framework for particle creation, Unruh radiation and Hawking radiation.","Field states and local observables are quantum while the spacetime metric is treated as a fixed classical background, with renormalized stress-energy connecting to semiclassical gravity.",["curved spacetime","Hawking","Unruh","semiclassical gravity"],["QFT in curved spacetime","QFTCS"],"theory / framework"),
    T("tomonaga-schwinger","Tomonaga–Schwinger covariant evolution",1946,"1940–1959","Formulations","established framework","The Tomonaga–Schwinger formalism generalizes Schrödinger evolution to state functionals associated with spacelike hypersurfaces, making relativistic interaction-picture evolution manifestly covariant.","Infinitesimal deformation of a spacelike hypersurface changes the state through the local interaction Hamiltonian density.",["relativistic QFT","hypersurface","covariance","interaction picture"],["Tomonaga–Schwinger equation"],"formulation"),
    T("higgs-mechanism","Brout–Englert–Higgs mechanism",1964,"1960–1979","Quantum field theory","established","Spontaneous symmetry breaking in a gauge theory can give gauge bosons mass while preserving the underlying gauge-theory consistency structure.","A field acquires a symmetry-breaking vacuum configuration; gauge fields couple to the resulting mode structure and obtain mass terms.",["Higgs","spontaneous symmetry breaking","gauge theory","Standard Model"],["BEH mechanism","Higgs mechanism"],"theory / framework"),
    T("grand-unification","Grand unified gauge theories",1974,"1960–1979","Quantum field theory","active research","Grand unified theories embed the Standard Model gauge factors into a larger gauge group so strong and electroweak interactions arise from one high-energy symmetry.","Quarks, leptons and gauge fields occupy unified multiplets above a symmetry-breaking scale, with proton decay and coupling relations among characteristic consequences.",["GUT","SU(5)","unification","particle physics"],["grand unified theory"],"theory family"),
    T("neutrino-mixing","Neutrino mixing and oscillation theory",1962,"1960–1979","Quantum field theory","established framework","Neutrino flavor states can be coherent superpositions of distinct mass eigenstates, producing oscillatory flavor-transition probabilities during propagation.","A unitary mixing matrix relates flavor and mass bases; relative phases accumulated by different masses generate flavor oscillations.",["neutrino","oscillation","PMNS","mixing"],["Pontecorvo–Maki–Nakagawa–Sakata mixing"],"theory / framework"),
    T("msw-effect","MSW matter effect",1978,"1960–1979","Quantum field theory","established framework","Coherent forward scattering in matter modifies effective neutrino mixing and can produce resonant flavor conversion.","Electron density changes the effective Hamiltonian for propagating neutrinos, shifting mixing angles and level splittings in matter.",["neutrino","matter effect","MSW","oscillation"],["Mikheyev–Smirnov–Wolfenstein effect"],"theory / framework"),
    T("seesaw-mechanism","Seesaw mechanism for neutrino mass",1977,"1960–1979","Quantum field theory","active research","Seesaw models explain very small neutrino masses by coupling ordinary neutrinos to much heavier neutral fermionic states.","Diagonalizing a mass matrix with a large Majorana scale can leave light neutrino eigenvalues suppressed approximately by the inverse heavy scale.",["neutrino mass","Majorana","seesaw","beyond Standard Model"],["type-I seesaw"],"theory / framework"),
    T("peccei-quinn","Peccei–Quinn mechanism",1977,"1960–1979","Quantum field theory","active research","The Peccei–Quinn mechanism promotes the strong-CP angle to a dynamical degree of freedom through an anomalous global chiral symmetry.","Spontaneous breaking of the Peccei–Quinn symmetry dynamically relaxes the effective QCD theta angle toward zero.",["strong CP","QCD","Peccei Quinn","axion"],[],"theory / framework"),
    T("axion","Axion theory",1978,"1960–1979","Quantum field theory","active research","The axion is the pseudo-Nambu–Goldstone boson associated with Peccei–Quinn symmetry breaking and is also a prominent dark-matter candidate in many models.","QCD effects generate a periodic axion potential whose minimum solves the strong-CP problem while leaving a light weakly coupled boson.",["axion","strong CP","dark matter","QCD"],[],"theory / framework"),
    T("finite-temperature-qft","Finite-temperature quantum field theory",1955,"1940–1959","Quantum field theory","established framework","Finite-temperature QFT extends field theory to thermal ensembles and is central to early-universe, plasma and relativistic many-body physics.","Correlation functions and effective actions are evaluated with thermal boundary conditions or real-time contours, introducing temperature-dependent propagators and collective effects.",["thermal field theory","Matsubara","real time","early universe"],["thermal quantum field theory"],"theory / framework"),
    T("black-hole-thermodynamics","Black-hole thermodynamics",1972,"1960–1979","Quantum gravity & spacetime","established framework","Black-hole mechanics together with quantum field theory assigns entropy proportional to horizon area and temperature proportional to surface gravity.","Horizon area behaves as thermodynamic entropy and Hawking radiation supplies the physical temperature, motivating the generalized second law.",["black holes","entropy","Bekenstein","Hawking"],[],"theory / framework"),
    T("black-hole-complementarity","Black-hole complementarity",1993,"1980–1999","Quantum gravity & spacetime","research proposal","Black-hole complementarity proposes that exterior and infalling descriptions are mutually consistent but cannot be combined into one operational account by a single observer.","Information can be encoded in stretched-horizon degrees of freedom for distant observers while infalling observers encounter ordinary horizon crossing, avoiding operational cloning.",["black hole information","complementarity","horizon","unitarity"],[],"research program"),
    T("fuzzball","Fuzzball microstate program",2002,"2000–2014","Quantum gravity & spacetime","active research","The fuzzball program in string theory replaces the conventional black-hole interior with horizon-scale quantum microstate structure intended to account microscopically for black-hole entropy and unitary evaporation.","Individual string-theoretic microstates are represented by nontrivial geometries or configurations rather than all sharing one featureless classical interior.",["fuzzball","string theory","microstates","black hole information"],["fuzzball proposal"],"research program"),
    T("amps-firewall","AMPS firewall argument",2012,"2000–2014","Quantum gravity & spacetime","foundational no-go argument","The AMPS argument sharpened the black-hole information problem by showing tension among late-radiation purity, low-energy effective field theory near the horizon, and a smooth infalling horizon.","Entanglement monogamy makes the expected near-horizon entanglement conflict with the entanglement needed to purify old Hawking radiation under the paper's assumptions.",["AMPS","firewall","black hole information","entanglement"],["black-hole firewall argument"],"no-go argument"),
    T("soft-hair","Soft-hair black-hole proposal",2016,"2015–present","Quantum gravity & spacetime","active research","The soft-hair proposal studies whether asymptotic and horizon soft charges associated with large gauge or BMS-like symmetries encode otherwise overlooked black-hole information.","Degenerate soft sectors can label black-hole states and alter the bookkeeping of information without by themselves constituting a complete evaporation model.",["soft hair","BMS symmetry","black holes","information"],[],"research program"),
    T("jt-gravity","Jackiw–Teitelboim gravity",1983,"1980–1999","Quantum gravity & spacetime","established toy framework","Jackiw–Teitelboim gravity is a two-dimensional dilaton-gravity theory that has become a controlled laboratory for near-AdS2 quantum gravity, black-hole thermodynamics and information-recovery calculations.","A dilaton enforces constant-curvature geometry while boundary dynamics capture important quantum-gravitational degrees of freedom.",["JT gravity","AdS2","dilaton","black holes"],["Jackiw-Teitelboim gravity"],"theory / framework"),
    T("postquantum-classical-gravity","Postquantum classical-gravity framework",2023,"2015–present","Quantum gravity & spacetime","active research","Oppenheim's postquantum framework explores consistent stochastic dynamics in which spacetime or gravity remains fundamentally classical while matter is quantum.","Classical degrees of freedom undergo stochastic evolution coupled to quantum matter, with the coupling inducing diffusion and decoherence constrained by consistency conditions.",["postquantum","classical gravity","hybrid dynamics","decoherence"],["postquantum theory of classical gravity"],"alternative theory"),
    T("configuration-ensemble-cq","Configuration-ensemble classical–quantum dynamics",2005,"2000–2014","Beyond standard quantum theory","active research","The Hall–Reginatto configuration-ensemble formalism describes classical, quantum and mixed classical–quantum systems using probability ensembles on a joint configuration space with canonically conjugate phase fields.","Classical and quantum sectors are distinguished by their ensemble Hamiltonians while interactions can include back-reaction and energy-conserving hybrid dynamics; the formalism has also been applied to quantum matter coupled to classical gravity.",["configuration ensemble","classical-quantum hybrid","Hall Reginatto","back-reaction","classical gravity"],["interacting classical and quantum ensembles","Hall–Reginatto hybrid theory"],"hybrid classical–quantum framework"),
    T("bmv-gravity-entanglement","Gravity-mediated entanglement witness proposals",2017,"2015–present","Quantum gravity & spacetime","active experimental framework","Bose–Marletto–Vedral type proposals use entanglement generated between spatially superposed masses as an operational probe of whether the mediating gravitational degrees of freedom require noncommuting observables under specified assumptions.","If two probes become entangled through only a local mediator, the mediator must possess enough nonclassical structure within the information-theoretic assumptions used by the proposals.",["BMV","gravity entanglement","quantum gravity test","interferometry"],["Bose–Marletto–Vedral proposal","gravity-induced entanglement"],"experimental framework"),
    T("kaluza-klein","Kaluza–Klein theory",1921,"1900–1924","Quantum gravity & spacetime","historical framework","Kaluza–Klein theory unifies gravity and gauge structure by extending spacetime with compact extra dimensions whose metric components appear as lower-dimensional fields.","Compactification of higher-dimensional gravity yields ordinary gravity together with gauge fields, scalar fields and towers of massive modes.",["extra dimensions","compactification","unification","Kaluza Klein"],[],"theory / framework"),
    T("braneworld-gravity","Braneworld gravity",1999,"1980–1999","Quantum gravity & spacetime","active research","Braneworld models place ordinary matter on a lower-dimensional brane embedded in a higher-dimensional bulk, allowing gravity to probe the extra dimensions.","Warped or large extra dimensions modify gravitational dynamics and can generate effective four-dimensional scales from higher-dimensional geometry.",["braneworld","extra dimensions","Randall Sundrum","gravity"],["brane-world gravity"],"theory family"),
    T("inflationary-cosmology","Inflationary cosmology",1981,"1980–1999","Astroparticle physics & cosmology","established framework","Inflationary cosmology posits an early phase of accelerated expansion that addresses horizon and flatness problems and provides a mechanism for generating primordial perturbations.","A near-vacuum-energy component drives quasi-exponential expansion before reheating into the hot Big Bang phase.",["inflation","early universe","cosmology","accelerated expansion"],["cosmic inflation"],"cosmological framework"),
    T("stochastic-inflation","Stochastic inflation",1986,"1980–1999","Astroparticle physics & cosmology","active framework","Stochastic inflation separates long- and short-wavelength field modes and represents the cumulative effect of horizon-crossing quantum fluctuations as stochastic noise acting on coarse-grained inflationary fields.","Long-wavelength inflaton dynamics obey an effective Langevin/Fokker–Planck description sourced by quantum fluctuations.",["inflation","stochastic","quantum fluctuations","Fokker Planck"],[],"cosmological framework"),
    T("reheating-preheating","Reheating and preheating after inflation",1982,"1980–1999","Astroparticle physics & cosmology","established framework","Reheating converts the energy stored in the inflationary sector into ordinary particles and radiation; preheating describes rapid nonperturbative particle production possible in some models.","Oscillating post-inflation fields can decay perturbatively or excite modes through parametric resonance before thermalization.",["reheating","preheating","inflation","particle production"],[],"cosmological framework"),
    T("lambda-cdm","ΛCDM cosmological model",1995,"1980–1999","Astroparticle physics & cosmology","established phenomenological model","ΛCDM is the standard phenomenological cosmological model combining general relativity, a cosmological constant, cold dark matter, baryons, radiation and primordial perturbations.","A small parameter set specifies the background expansion and primordial spectrum used to predict CMB, large-scale-structure and distance observables.",["Lambda CDM","dark matter","dark energy","cosmology"],["Lambda-CDM","standard cosmological model"],"cosmological model"),
    T("quintessence","Quintessence dark-energy models",1988,"1980–1999","Astroparticle physics & cosmology","active research","Quintessence models replace a strict cosmological constant with a slowly evolving scalar field whose potential energy can drive late-time accelerated expansion.","A light scalar rolls on a sufficiently flat potential, producing a time-dependent equation of state distinct from a fixed cosmological constant.",["dark energy","scalar field","accelerated expansion","quintessence"],[],"cosmological framework"),
    T("mond","Modified Newtonian dynamics (MOND)",1983,"1980–1999","Astroparticle physics & cosmology","alternative phenomenology","MOND proposes a modification of low-acceleration dynamics designed to reproduce galaxy-scale regularities without invoking conventional particle dark matter at those scales.","Below a characteristic acceleration scale, the effective gravitational relation departs from the Newtonian form.",["MOND","modified gravity","galaxy dynamics","dark matter alternative"],[],"phenomenological framework"),
    T("teves","Tensor–vector–scalar gravity (TeVeS)",2004,"2000–2014","Astroparticle physics & cosmology","alternative gravity theory","TeVeS is a relativistic tensor–vector–scalar gravity theory constructed to reproduce MOND-like behavior in an appropriate limit while supporting relativistic lensing and cosmological calculations.","Metric, vector and scalar fields combine to modify gravitational dynamics and recover MOND phenomenology in the weak-acceleration regime.",["TeVeS","MOND","modified gravity","relativistic gravity"],[],"alternative theory"),
    T("wimp-dark-matter","WIMP dark-matter paradigm",1980,"1980–1999","Astroparticle physics & cosmology","candidate framework","Weakly interacting massive particle models posit stable or long-lived massive particles with interactions near the weak scale as a possible microscopic realization of cold dark matter.","Thermal freeze-out can leave a relic abundance set by the annihilation cross section, motivating collider, indirect and direct-detection searches.",["WIMP","dark matter","freeze-out","astroparticle"],[],"candidate framework"),
    T("fuzzy-dark-matter","Fuzzy / ultralight scalar dark matter",2000,"2000–2014","Astroparticle physics & cosmology","candidate framework","Fuzzy dark matter uses an ultralight bosonic field whose macroscopic de Broglie wavelength modifies structure on galactic scales while behaving approximately as dark matter cosmologically.","Wave pressure and field coherence suppress small-scale clustering below a characteristic scale set by the particle mass.",["fuzzy dark matter","ultralight boson","wave dark matter","structure formation"],["wave dark matter"],"candidate framework"),
    T("self-interacting-dark-matter","Self-interacting dark matter",2000,"2000–2014","Astroparticle physics & cosmology","candidate framework","Self-interacting dark-matter models allow appreciable dark-sector scattering that can alter halo cores and substructure while preserving large-scale cold-dark-matter behavior.","Dark-matter particles exchange momentum through non-negligible self-scattering, changing halo thermodynamics and density profiles.",["SIDM","dark matter","self interaction","halos"],[],"candidate framework"),
    T("primordial-black-hole-dark-matter","Primordial-black-hole dark matter",1974,"1960–1979","Astroparticle physics & cosmology","candidate framework","Primordial black holes formed in the early universe can contribute some fraction of the dark-matter density, subject to mass-dependent observational constraints.","Enhanced early-universe density fluctuations or other mechanisms can collapse into black holes before stellar formation, producing a nonparticle dark-matter candidate.",["primordial black holes","dark matter","early universe","PBH"],[],"candidate framework"),
    T("leptogenesis","Leptogenesis",1986,"1980–1999","Astroparticle physics & cosmology","active mechanism","Leptogenesis explains the cosmic baryon asymmetry by first generating a lepton asymmetry, commonly through CP-violating decays of heavy Majorana neutrinos, and then partially converting it to baryon number.","Out-of-equilibrium lepton-number and CP-violating processes create an asymmetry that electroweak sphalerons reprocess into baryon number.",["leptogenesis","baryogenesis","neutrino","CP violation"],[],"cosmological mechanism"),
    T("sakharov-baryogenesis","Sakharov baryogenesis conditions",1967,"1960–1979","Astroparticle physics & cosmology","established framework","Sakharov identified baryon-number violation, C/CP violation and departure from thermal equilibrium as the classic conditions under which microphysics can generate a cosmic matter–antimatter asymmetry.","A dynamical early-universe process satisfying the Sakharov conditions can evolve an initially symmetric state into a net baryon excess.",["baryogenesis","Sakharov","CP violation","early universe"],[],"foundational framework"),
    T("cosmic-strings","Cosmic strings and topological-defect theory",1976,"1960–1979","Astroparticle physics & cosmology","active framework","Cosmic strings are line-like topological defects that can form during symmetry-breaking phase transitions in field theories and can leave gravitational and cosmological signatures.","Nontrivial vacuum topology can trap field configurations into stable or long-lived string defects with tension set by the symmetry-breaking scale.",["cosmic strings","topological defects","phase transition","early universe"],[],"cosmological framework"),
    T("fermi-liquid","Landau Fermi-liquid theory",1957,"1940–1959","Quantum many-body & condensed matter","established framework","Landau Fermi-liquid theory describes interacting fermions at low energy in terms of long-lived quasiparticles continuously connected to those of a free Fermi gas.","Interactions renormalize quasiparticle parameters and introduce residual Landau interactions while preserving a sharp Fermi surface in the regime of validity.",["Fermi liquid","quasiparticles","Fermi surface","many body"],[],"theory / framework"),
    T("luttinger-liquid","Luttinger-liquid theory",1981,"1980–1999","Quantum many-body & condensed matter","established framework","Luttinger-liquid theory describes broad classes of interacting one-dimensional quantum fluids whose low-energy behavior is not that of a Landau Fermi liquid.","Collective bosonic modes replace electron-like quasiparticles and correlation functions show interaction-dependent power laws.",["Luttinger liquid","one dimension","bosonization","correlations"],[],"theory / framework"),
    T("bose-hubbard","Bose–Hubbard model",1989,"1980–1999","Quantum many-body & condensed matter","established framework","The Bose–Hubbard model describes interacting bosons hopping on a lattice and supports superfluid and Mott-insulating phases.","Competition between kinetic hopping and on-site repulsion drives a quantum phase transition between delocalized and number-localized regimes.",["Bose Hubbard","Mott insulator","superfluid","lattice bosons"],[],"model"),
    T("heisenberg-spin-model","Heisenberg quantum spin model",1928,"1925–1939","Quantum many-body & condensed matter","established framework","The Heisenberg model describes localized quantum spins coupled by exchange interactions and underlies much of quantum magnetism.","Neighboring spin operators interact through rotationally symmetric exchange, producing ferro- or antiferromagnetic correlations depending on the coupling.",["Heisenberg model","quantum magnetism","spin","exchange"],[],"model"),
    T("transverse-ising","Transverse-field Ising model",1970,"1960–1979","Quantum many-body & condensed matter","established framework","The transverse-field Ising model combines Ising interactions with a noncommuting transverse field and is a canonical model of quantum criticality.","Competition between interaction-aligned order and transverse quantum fluctuations produces a zero-temperature phase transition.",["Ising","quantum criticality","spin model","transverse field"],[],"model"),
    T("kitaev-honeycomb","Kitaev honeycomb model",2006,"2000–2014","Quantum many-body & condensed matter","established framework","The Kitaev honeycomb model is an exactly solvable spin model with bond-dependent interactions whose excitations can be represented using Majorana fermions and emergent gauge fields.","Directional spin couplings on a honeycomb lattice generate quantum-spin-liquid phases, including a non-Abelian topological phase under suitable perturbations.",["Kitaev","honeycomb","spin liquid","Majorana"],[],"model"),
    T("aklt","AKLT valence-bond-solid model",1987,"1980–1999","Quantum many-body & condensed matter","established framework","The Affleck–Kennedy–Lieb–Tasaki model provides an exactly solvable spin chain with a valence-bond-solid ground state and a finite excitation gap.","Spin-1 degrees of freedom can be represented by symmetrized virtual spin-1/2 pairs forming neighboring singlet bonds.",["AKLT","valence bond solid","Haldane phase","spin chain"],[],"model"),
    T("topological-insulator","Z₂ topological-insulator theory",2005,"2000–2014","Quantum many-body & condensed matter","established framework","Time-reversal-invariant band structures can possess a Z₂ topological invariant that protects boundary states without an external magnetic field.","Spin–orbit coupling can produce a bulk insulating phase whose edge or surface modes are protected by time-reversal symmetry.",["topological insulator","Z2","quantum spin Hall","band topology"],[],"theory / framework"),
    T("topological-superconductor","Topological-superconductor / Majorana-chain framework",2001,"2000–2014","Quantum many-body & condensed matter","established framework","Topological superconductors pair fermions in a phase that supports boundary Majorana zero modes and nontrivial bulk topological invariants.","A gapped superconducting bulk can protect zero-energy Majorana boundary excitations whose occupation is encoded nonlocally.",["topological superconductor","Majorana","Kitaev chain","BdG"],["Majorana chain"],"theory / framework"),
    T("rvb-spin-liquid","RVB quantum-spin-liquid framework",1973,"1960–1979","Quantum many-body & condensed matter","active framework","Resonating-valence-bond theory describes quantum magnets through superpositions of different singlet-bond coverings and helped motivate modern quantum-spin-liquid theory.","Strong quantum fluctuations can prevent conventional magnetic order while maintaining long-range entanglement among fluctuating singlet bonds.",["RVB","spin liquid","valence bonds","Anderson"],["resonating valence bond"],"theory / framework"),
    T("bethe-ansatz","Bethe-ansatz framework",1931,"1925–1939","Quantum many-body & condensed matter","established method","The Bethe ansatz solves selected one-dimensional interacting quantum models by representing many-body eigenstates through factorized plane-wave amplitudes constrained by algebraic equations.","Integrability permits many-body scattering to factorize so spectra are determined by coupled Bethe equations for rapidities or momenta.",["Bethe ansatz","integrability","one dimension","exact solution"],[],"exact-solution framework"),
    T("quantum-phase-transitions","Quantum phase-transition theory",1976,"1960–1979","Quantum many-body & condensed matter","established framework","Quantum phase transitions are zero-temperature transitions driven by nonthermal control parameters and governed by quantum fluctuations.","Near a quantum critical point, spatial and temporal correlations become scale dependent and can often be described by quantum critical scaling theories.",["quantum criticality","phase transition","scaling","many body"],[],"theory / framework"),
    T("born-oppenheimer","Born–Oppenheimer approximation",1927,"1925–1939","Quantum chemistry & electronic structure","established approximation","The Born–Oppenheimer framework exploits the large nuclear-to-electron mass ratio to separate fast electronic motion from slower nuclear motion to leading order.","Molecular wavefunctions are approximately factorized into electronic states parametrized by nuclear coordinates and nuclear wavefunctions evolving on potential-energy surfaces.",["Born Oppenheimer","molecules","electronic structure","nuclear motion"],[],"approximation framework"),
    T("valence-bond","Valence-bond theory",1927,"1925–1939","Quantum chemistry & electronic structure","established framework","Valence-bond theory describes chemical bonding using localized atomic-like orbitals and spin-coupled electron-pair structures.","Molecular states are expanded in localized bonding structures whose quantum superposition and exchange stabilize covalent bonds.",["valence bond","Heitler London","chemical bonding","localized orbitals"],[],"theory / framework"),
    T("molecular-orbital","Molecular-orbital theory",1932,"1925–1939","Quantum chemistry & electronic structure","established framework","Molecular-orbital theory represents electrons in orbitals delocalized over an entire molecule and builds many-electron states from their occupations.","Atomic-orbital basis functions combine into molecular orbitals that are occupied according to the electronic state and symmetry.",["molecular orbital","Mulliken","chemical bonding","delocalization"],[],"theory / framework"),
    T("casscf","CASSCF multiconfigurational theory",1980,"1980–1999","Quantum chemistry & electronic structure","established framework","Complete-active-space self-consistent-field theory optimizes both orbitals and a full configuration-interaction expansion within a chosen active orbital subspace.","Strongly correlated valence configurations are treated variationally inside an active space while inactive and virtual orbitals are optimized self-consistently.",["CASSCF","multireference","active space","electronic structure"],[],"computational framework"),
    T("random-phase-approximation","Random-phase approximation",1953,"1940–1959","Quantum chemistry & electronic structure","established framework","The random-phase approximation sums a characteristic class of collective screening and density-response contributions and appears in both many-body physics and electronic-structure theory.","Linearized self-consistent response or ring-diagram resummation describes collective excitations and screened correlations around a reference state.",["RPA","screening","response","many body"],[],"approximation framework"),
    T("dmet","Density-matrix embedding theory",2012,"2000–2014","Quantum chemistry & electronic structure","active framework","Density-matrix embedding theory maps a large interacting system onto quantum impurity problems coupled to a compact bath chosen to reproduce reduced-density information.","A self-consistent low-level lattice or molecular state defines bath orbitals for high-level correlated calculations on selected fragments.",["DMET","embedding","strong correlation","electronic structure"],[],"computational framework"),
    T("dicke-model","Dicke model",1954,"1940–1959","Quantum optics & AMO","established framework","The Dicke model describes many two-level systems collectively coupled to a common quantized radiation mode and exhibits cooperative light–matter phenomena.","Collective spin operators couple an ensemble of emitters to a single bosonic field mode, generalizing single-emitter light–matter models.",["Dicke","superradiance","light matter","collective"],[],"model"),
    T("tavis-cummings","Tavis–Cummings model",1968,"1960–1979","Quantum optics & AMO","established framework","The Tavis–Cummings model is the rotating-wave many-emitter extension of the Jaynes–Cummings model.","An ensemble of two-level systems exchanges excitations collectively with a single quantized cavity mode while counter-rotating terms are neglected.",["Tavis Cummings","cavity QED","collective coupling","rotating wave"],[],"model"),
    T("cavity-qed","Cavity quantum electrodynamics",1980,"1980–1999","Quantum optics & AMO","established framework","Cavity QED studies quantized light interacting with atoms or other emitters in resonators that reshape the electromagnetic mode density and enhance coherent coupling.","Strong confinement can make coherent emitter–photon exchange dominate dissipation, enabling direct tests and control of light–matter quantum dynamics.",["cavity QED","strong coupling","cavity","light matter"],[],"theory / framework"),
    T("circuit-qed","Circuit quantum electrodynamics",2004,"2000–2014","Quantum optics & AMO","established framework","Circuit QED realizes cavity-QED physics with superconducting artificial atoms coupled to quantized microwave resonators on a chip.","Engineered circuits provide tunable strong light–matter coupling, dispersive readout and nonlinear interactions for quantum information processing.",["circuit QED","superconducting qubits","microwave resonator","quantum information"],[],"theory / framework"),
    T("floquet-quantum","Floquet quantum theory",1965,"1960–1979","Quantum optics & AMO","established framework","Floquet theory treats quantum systems driven periodically in time using quasienergy states analogous to Bloch states in spatially periodic systems.","For a periodic Hamiltonian, solutions separate into a phase generated by quasienergy and a state periodic with the drive period.",["Floquet","periodic driving","quasienergy","nonequilibrium"],["Floquet quantum mechanics"],"formulation"),
    T("rydberg-blockade","Rydberg-blockade quantum dynamics",2000,"2000–2014","Quantum optics & AMO","established framework","Strong interactions between highly excited Rydberg atoms can prevent nearby atoms from being excited simultaneously, producing a controllable blockade constraint.","Within a blockade radius, an existing Rydberg excitation shifts neighboring transition energies enough to suppress additional resonant excitation.",["Rydberg blockade","neutral atoms","quantum gates","strong interactions"],[],"theory / framework"),
    T("laser-cooling","Laser-cooling theory",1975,"1960–1979","Quantum optics & AMO","established framework","Laser cooling uses momentum exchange and frequency-selective light scattering to reduce the kinetic energy of atoms and ions, with Doppler and sub-Doppler regimes described by quantum optical theory.","Velocity-dependent photon absorption plus spontaneous emission produces a net damping force and, with suitable level structure, temperatures below the simple Doppler limit.",["laser cooling","Doppler cooling","atoms","quantum optics"],[],"theory / framework"),

    T("scalar-tensor-gravity","Scalar–tensor gravity",1961,"1960–1979","Quantum gravity & spacetime","active theory family","Scalar–tensor gravity extends metric gravity by adding one or more dynamical scalar fields coupled to spacetime curvature and matter.","The gravitational interaction is carried by the metric together with scalar degrees of freedom whose couplings can vary across specific models.",["modified gravity","scalar tensor","gravity","cosmology"],[],"theory family"),
    T("brans-dicke","Brans–Dicke gravity",1961,"1960–1979","Quantum gravity & spacetime","established alternative gravity theory","Brans–Dicke theory is the canonical scalar–tensor extension of general relativity, introducing a dynamical scalar that controls the effective gravitational coupling.","A scalar field multiplies the Ricci curvature in the action and has a kinetic term governed by the Brans–Dicke parameter.",["Brans Dicke","scalar tensor","modified gravity","Mach principle"],[],"alternative theory"),
    T("f-r-gravity","f(R) gravity",1980,"1980–1999","Quantum gravity & spacetime","active theory family","f(R) gravity replaces the Einstein–Hilbert Ricci-scalar Lagrangian with a nonlinear function of the Ricci scalar and is a major modified-gravity family in cosmology.","The metric field equations acquire additional curvature-dependent terms and can be recast in scalar–tensor form under broad conditions.",["f(R)","modified gravity","dark energy","inflation"],[],"theory family"),
    T("horndeski-gravity","Horndeski gravity",1974,"1960–1979","Quantum gravity & spacetime","active theory family","Horndeski theory is the most general four-dimensional single-scalar metric theory with second-order Euler–Lagrange field equations in its original formulation.","Specific choices of the free functions reproduce or extend many scalar–tensor and dark-energy models while controlling additional degrees of freedom.",["Horndeski","scalar tensor","modified gravity","dark energy"],[],"theory family"),
    T("dgp-gravity","Dvali–Gabadadze–Porrati gravity",2000,"2000–2014","Quantum gravity & spacetime","active research","The DGP model embeds a four-dimensional brane in an infinite five-dimensional bulk so gravity crosses over from effectively four- to five-dimensional behavior at large distances.","An induced four-dimensional curvature term on the brane competes with five-dimensional bulk gravity, producing scale-dependent gravitational propagation.",["DGP","braneworld","extra dimensions","modified gravity"],[],"alternative theory"),
    T("massive-gravity-drgt","dRGT ghost-free massive gravity",2011,"2000–2014","Quantum gravity & spacetime","active research","de Rham–Gabadadze–Tolley massive gravity gives the graviton a nonlinear interaction potential arranged to avoid the Boulware–Deser ghost in the fully developed theory.","A reference metric and tuned nonlinear potential terms break the massless-graviton gauge structure while propagating the degrees of freedom of a massive spin-2 field.",["dRGT","massive gravity","graviton mass","modified gravity"],["ghost-free massive gravity"],"alternative theory"),
    T("einstein-aether","Einstein–Æther gravity",2001,"2000–2014","Quantum gravity & spacetime","active research","Einstein–Æther theory adds a dynamical unit timelike vector field to gravity, introducing a locally preferred frame while retaining general covariance.","The metric couples to a constrained timelike vector whose derivative terms generate additional spin-0 and spin-1 gravitational modes.",["Einstein Aether","Lorentz violation","preferred frame","modified gravity"],[],"alternative theory"),
