    T("galileon-gravity","Galileon gravity",2009,"2000–2014","Quantum gravity & spacetime","active research","Galileon theories use derivative self-interactions of a scalar field with a symmetry inherited from the DGP decoupling limit and can modify gravity while retaining second-order equations in the original construction.","Nonlinear derivative interactions activate the Vainshtein screening mechanism, suppressing deviations from general relativity near dense sources.",["Galileon","Vainshtein","modified gravity","scalar field"],[],"theory family"),
    T("dhost-gravity","DHOST gravity",2016,"2015–present","Quantum gravity & spacetime","active research","Degenerate higher-order scalar–tensor theories extend Horndeski-type models while using degeneracy conditions to remove the extra Ostrogradsky degree of freedom that generic higher-derivative theories would carry.","The higher-derivative Lagrangian is constrained so its kinetic matrix is degenerate, leaving the intended scalar and tensor propagating modes.",["DHOST","beyond Horndeski","degeneracy","modified gravity"],["degenerate higher-order scalar–tensor theory"],"theory family"),
    T("sterile-neutrino-dark-matter","Sterile-neutrino dark matter",1994,"1980–1999","Astroparticle physics & cosmology","candidate framework","Sterile-neutrino dark-matter models add gauge-singlet neutrinos whose small mixing with active neutrinos can generate a cosmological relic population.","Production through early-universe neutrino mixing can yield nonthermal warm or colder dark matter depending on masses, mixing and cosmological history.",["sterile neutrino","dark matter","warm dark matter","neutrino"],[],"candidate framework"),
    T("dark-photon","Dark-photon / kinetic-mixing framework",1986,"1980–1999","Astroparticle physics & cosmology","active framework","Dark-photon models introduce an additional U(1) gauge field that can interact weakly with the Standard Model through kinetic mixing with hypercharge or electromagnetism.","Diagonalizing mixed Abelian kinetic terms gives hidden-sector states small effective couplings to electrically charged matter.",["dark photon","kinetic mixing","hidden sector","U(1)"],[],"theory / framework"),
    T("freeze-in-dark-matter","Freeze-in dark-matter production",2010,"2000–2014","Astroparticle physics & cosmology","active mechanism","Freeze-in produces dark matter from extremely feeble interactions with a thermal bath so the dark species never reaches thermal equilibrium.","Rare decays or scatterings gradually populate feebly interacting massive particles, with the relic yield accumulating while interaction rates remain below equilibration.",["freeze-in","FIMP","dark matter","relic abundance"],[],"cosmological mechanism"),
    T("asymmetric-dark-matter","Asymmetric dark matter",2009,"2000–2014","Astroparticle physics & cosmology","active framework","Asymmetric-dark-matter models relate the surviving dark-matter abundance to a particle–antiparticle asymmetry, often connected to the baryon or lepton asymmetry.","Efficient annihilation removes the symmetric component while a conserved or transferred dark-sector asymmetry sets the relic density.",["asymmetric dark matter","baryogenesis","dark sector","relic abundance"],[],"candidate framework"),
    T("affleck-dine-baryogenesis","Affleck–Dine baryogenesis",1985,"1980–1999","Astroparticle physics & cosmology","active mechanism","Affleck–Dine baryogenesis uses the coherent evolution of scalar fields carrying baryon or lepton number, especially along flat directions in supersymmetric theories, to generate the cosmic asymmetry.","A displaced complex scalar condensate evolves with baryon-number and CP-violating interactions, producing a net charge before decaying into ordinary particles.",["Affleck Dine","baryogenesis","supersymmetry","early universe"],[],"cosmological mechanism"),
    T("schwinger-model","Schwinger model",1962,"1960–1979","Quantum field theory","established model","The Schwinger model is exactly solvable quantum electrodynamics in 1+1 dimensions and demonstrates dynamical gauge-boson mass generation and confinement-like behavior.","A massless Dirac field coupled to an Abelian gauge field in two dimensions can be solved nonperturbatively and maps to a massive bosonic degree of freedom.",["Schwinger model","QED2","exact solution","bosonization"],[],"model"),
    T("thirring-model","Thirring model",1958,"1940–1959","Quantum field theory","established model","The Thirring model is a soluble 1+1-dimensional relativistic fermion theory with a local current–current self-interaction.","The four-fermion interaction admits exact and bosonized treatments and provides a canonical laboratory for interacting relativistic field theory.",["Thirring","integrable QFT","four fermion","bosonization"],[],"model"),
    T("gross-neveu-model","Gross–Neveu model",1974,"1960–1979","Quantum field theory","established model","The Gross–Neveu model is an asymptotically free two-dimensional fermion field theory exhibiting dynamical mass generation and symmetry breaking in large-N treatments.","Quartically interacting fermions generate a mass scale dynamically despite a classically scale-free massless Lagrangian.",["Gross Neveu","asymptotic freedom","large N","dynamical symmetry breaking"],[],"model"),
    T("njl-model","Nambu–Jona-Lasinio model",1961,"1960–1979","Quantum field theory","established model","The Nambu–Jona-Lasinio model describes interacting fermions with contact interactions and provided an influential field-theoretic model of dynamical chiral-symmetry breaking.","A four-fermion interaction can generate a fermion condensate and an effective mass through a gap equation analogous to BCS superconductivity.",["NJL","chiral symmetry breaking","four fermion","QCD model"],[],"model"),
    T("chern-simons-qft","Chern–Simons quantum field theory",1989,"1980–1999","Quantum field theory","established framework","Chern–Simons theory is a three-dimensional topological gauge theory whose quantum observables encode knot and three-manifold invariants and that underlies effective descriptions of anyons and quantum Hall phases.","The action depends on a gauge connection but not a spacetime metric, so gauge-invariant observables capture global topological information.",["Chern Simons","TQFT","anyons","knot invariants"],[],"topological field theory"),
    T("bf-theory","BF topological field theory",1991,"1980–1999","Quantum field theory","established framework","BF theories are topological gauge theories built from a curvature two-form coupled to an auxiliary differential form and appear in topological field theory and formulations of gravity.","The metric-independent BF action constrains gauge curvature and supports topological observables, with constrained variants related to gravitational theories.",["BF theory","TQFT","gauge theory","topology"],[],"topological field theory"),
    T("wzw-model","Wess–Zumino–Witten model",1984,"1980–1999","Quantum field theory","established framework","Wess–Zumino–Witten models are two-dimensional conformal field theories on group manifolds with a topological Wess–Zumino term and affine current algebra symmetry.","The sigma-model action plus quantized Wess–Zumino term produces exactly constrained conformal dynamics and realizes non-Abelian bosonization.",["WZW","conformal field theory","current algebra","bosonization"],["Wess-Zumino-Witten model"],"conformal field theory"),
    T("bkt-transition","Berezinskii–Kosterlitz–Thouless transition",1973,"1960–1979","Quantum many-body & condensed matter","established framework","The BKT framework describes a topological phase transition in two-dimensional systems driven by binding and unbinding of vortex–antivortex pairs rather than conventional symmetry-breaking order.","At low temperature vortices remain bound and correlations decay algebraically; proliferation of free vortices above the transition destroys quasi-long-range order.",["BKT","vortices","topological transition","XY model"],["Kosterlitz-Thouless transition"],"theory / framework"),
    T("haldane-phase","Haldane integer-spin-chain theory",1983,"1980–1999","Quantum many-body & condensed matter","established framework","Haldane showed that one-dimensional antiferromagnetic Heisenberg chains have qualitatively different low-energy behavior for integer and half-integer spin, with integer-spin chains generically gapped.","Mapping the spin chain to a nonlinear sigma model with a topological term distinguishes integer and half-integer spin sectors.",["Haldane conjecture","spin chain","sigma model","topological phase"],[],"theory / framework"),
    T("composite-fermions","Composite-fermion theory",1989,"1980–1999","Quantum many-body & condensed matter","established framework","Composite-fermion theory reorganizes the fractional quantum Hall effect in terms of electrons bound to an even number of flux quanta, mapping many fractional states to effective integer quantum Hall states.","Flux attachment changes the effective magnetic field seen by emergent composite fermions and produces the observed hierarchy of filling fractions.",["composite fermion","fractional quantum Hall","Jain","flux attachment"],[],"theory / framework"),
    T("symmetry-protected-topological","Symmetry-protected topological phases",2011,"2000–2014","Quantum many-body & condensed matter","established framework","SPT theory classifies gapped short-range-entangled phases that are distinct only when specified protecting symmetries are preserved.","The bulk has no intrinsic topological order, but symmetry prevents adiabatic deformation to a trivial product state and protects characteristic boundary structure.",["SPT","topological phase","symmetry","short-range entanglement"],[],"classification framework"),
    T("u1-spin-liquid","U(1) quantum-spin-liquid framework",2004,"2000–2014","Quantum many-body & condensed matter","active framework","U(1) quantum spin liquids exhibit emergent compact gauge structure with fractionalized matter excitations and, in three dimensions, photon-like gapless collective modes.","Local spin constraints generate an emergent gauge field whose deconfined phase supports spinons, monopole defects and gauge-photon excitations.",["U1 spin liquid","emergent gauge field","spinons","frustration"],[],"theory / framework"),
    T("caspt2","CASPT2 multireference perturbation theory",1990,"1980–1999","Quantum chemistry & electronic structure","established framework","CASPT2 adds second-order perturbative dynamical-correlation corrections to a CASSCF multiconfigurational reference.","A zeroth-order Hamiltonian defined from the active-space reference generates a second-order correction from configurations outside the complete active space.",["CASPT2","multireference","perturbation theory","CASSCF"],[],"computational framework"),
    T("nevpt2","NEVPT2 multireference perturbation theory",2001,"2000–2014","Quantum chemistry & electronic structure","established framework","NEVPT2 is a second-order multireference perturbation theory built from an n-electron valence active-space reference and a Dyall-type zeroth-order Hamiltonian.","Strongly or partially contracted external spaces provide size-consistent dynamic-correlation corrections with favorable intruder-state behavior.",["NEVPT2","multireference","Dyall Hamiltonian","CASSCF"],[],"computational framework"),
    T("eom-cc","Equation-of-motion coupled-cluster theory",1993,"1980–1999","Quantum chemistry & electronic structure","established framework","EOM-CC obtains excited, ionized or electron-attached states by diagonalizing a similarity-transformed Hamiltonian in an excitation operator space built on a coupled-cluster reference.","Linear excitation operators acting on the correlated reference convert the ground-state coupled-cluster problem into a non-Hermitian eigenvalue problem for target states.",["EOM-CC","coupled cluster","excited states","electronic structure"],[],"computational framework"),
    T("adc","Algebraic-diagrammatic construction",1982,"1980–1999","Quantum chemistry & electronic structure","established framework","ADC reorganizes perturbation theory for polarization or one-particle propagators into finite Hermitian or structured matrix eigenvalue problems for excitation and ionization spectra.","Perturbative moment matching generates systematically improvable effective matrices whose poles approximate correlated electronic excitation energies.",["ADC","propagator","excited states","Green function"],[],"computational framework"),
    T("gf2","Self-consistent second-order Green-function theory (GF2)",2014,"2000–2014","Quantum chemistry & electronic structure","active framework","GF2 solves the Dyson equation self-consistently using a second-order skeleton self-energy and can treat weak-to-moderate correlation without choosing a single broken-symmetry determinant.","Imaginary-time and imaginary-frequency Green functions are iterated with the second-order self-energy until one-particle dynamics and density become self-consistent.",["GF2","Green function","Dyson equation","electronic structure"],[],"computational framework"),
    T("dmrg-scf","DMRG-SCF electronic-structure method",2008,"2000–2014","Quantum chemistry & electronic structure","established framework","DMRG-SCF combines density-matrix renormalization group treatment of a large active space with self-consistent orbital optimization, extending CASSCF-style multiconfigurational calculations to larger active spaces.","The active-space wavefunction is represented by a matrix-product state and optimized together with molecular orbitals in a variational cycle.",["DMRG-SCF","DMRG","active space","orbital optimization"],[],"computational framework"),
    T("quantum-optomechanics","Quantum cavity optomechanics",2007,"2000–2014","Quantum optics & AMO","established framework","Quantum optomechanics studies coherent and dissipative coupling between quantized electromagnetic cavity fields and mechanical motion through radiation pressure or equivalent interactions.","Photon number shifts a mechanical coordinate while motion shifts the cavity resonance, enabling cooling, state transfer, squeezing and quantum-limited measurement.",["optomechanics","cavity","mechanical oscillator","quantum measurement"],[],"theory / framework"),
    T("eit","Electromagnetically induced transparency",1990,"1980–1999","Quantum optics & AMO","established framework","EIT uses destructive quantum interference among driven atomic transition pathways to make an otherwise absorbing medium transparent in a narrow spectral window.","A coherent control field creates a dark-state superposition that suppresses excitation of the lossy intermediate level and strongly modifies dispersion.",["EIT","coherent population trapping","dark state","quantum optics"],[],"theory / framework"),
    T("stirap","Stimulated Raman adiabatic passage",1990,"1980–1999","Quantum optics & AMO","established framework","STIRAP transfers population between quantum states by adiabatically following a dark eigenstate created by counterintuitively ordered pump and Stokes pulses.","Overlapping control pulses rotate the dark state from the initial to target level while keeping the lossy intermediate state weakly populated.",["STIRAP","adiabatic passage","dark state","coherent control"],[],"control framework"),
    T("trapped-ion-qc","Trapped-ion quantum-computing architecture",1995,"1980–1999","Quantum information & open systems","established framework","Trapped-ion quantum computing encodes qubits in long-lived ionic states and uses shared quantized motional modes plus laser interactions to implement entangling gates.","Internal-state qubits are coherently coupled through collective motion, providing a controllable architecture for universal quantum logic and precision measurement.",["trapped ions","quantum computing","Cirac Zoller","quantum gates"],[],"computing architecture"),
    T("optical-lattice-quantum-simulation","Optical-lattice quantum simulation",1998,"1980–1999","Quantum optics & AMO","established framework","Ultracold atoms in optical lattices realize tunable lattice Hamiltonians such as the Bose–Hubbard model and provide a controlled platform for quantum simulation of many-body phases.","Standing-wave light creates periodic potentials whose depth and interactions tune hopping, on-site interactions and the superfluid–Mott transition.",["optical lattice","quantum simulation","Bose Hubbard","ultracold atoms"],[],"experimental framework"),

    T("quantum-chaos","Quantum chaos",1984,"1980–1999","Quantum many-body & condensed matter","established framework","Quantum-chaos theory studies signatures of classically chaotic dynamics and nonintegrability in quantum spectra, eigenstates and time evolution.","Spectral statistics, semiclassical orbit structure and random-matrix universality diagnose quantum systems without conventional conserved quantities.",["quantum chaos","random matrix theory","spectral statistics","semiclassical"],[],"theory / framework"),
    T("eigenstate-thermalization","Eigenstate thermalization hypothesis",1991,"1980–1999","Quantum many-body & condensed matter","active framework","ETH explains thermalization in generic isolated many-body quantum systems by asserting that matrix elements of simple observables have a smooth thermodynamic structure in the energy eigenbasis.","Individual many-body eigenstates can reproduce equilibrium expectation values for local observables when the ETH ansatz applies.",["ETH","thermalization","quantum chaos","statistical mechanics"],[],"foundational framework"),
    T("many-body-localization","Many-body localization",2006,"2000–2014","Quantum many-body & condensed matter","active framework","Many-body localization describes interacting disordered quantum systems that can fail to thermalize and retain long-lived memory of local initial conditions.","Quasilocal integrals of motion and inhibited transport stabilize a nonergodic phase that violates the usual ETH description.",["MBL","localization","thermalization","disorder"],[],"theory / framework"),
    T("generalized-gibbs-ensemble","Generalized Gibbs ensemble",2007,"2000–2014","Quantum many-body & condensed matter","established framework","The generalized Gibbs ensemble describes stationary properties of integrable quantum systems by constraining the full relevant set of conserved quantities rather than energy alone.","Maximum entropy subject to many conserved charges yields an equilibrium-like ensemble appropriate to integrable dynamics after relaxation.",["GGE","integrability","thermalization","conserved charges"],[],"statistical framework"),
    T("quantum-fluctuation-relations","Quantum fluctuation relations",1997,"1980–1999","Quantum information & open systems","established framework","Quantum fluctuation relations extend nonequilibrium work and entropy-production identities such as Jarzynski and Crooks relations to quantum systems and measurement protocols.","Forward and reverse nonequilibrium trajectory statistics obey exact identities connecting work distributions to equilibrium free-energy differences under specified dynamics and measurements.",["Jarzynski","Crooks","nonequilibrium","quantum thermodynamics"],[],"thermodynamic framework"),
    T("spin-boson","Spin–boson model",1981,"1980–1999","Quantum many-body & condensed matter","established model","The spin–boson model represents a two-level quantum system linearly coupled to a bath of harmonic oscillators and is a canonical model of dissipation and decoherence.","A pseudospin tunneling Hamiltonian couples to a continuum of bosonic environmental modes whose spectral density controls relaxation and localization behavior.",["spin boson","dissipation","open systems","decoherence"],[],"model"),
    T("caldeira-leggett","Caldeira–Leggett quantum Brownian motion",1983,"1980–1999","Quantum information & open systems","established model","The Caldeira–Leggett framework models a distinguished quantum coordinate coupled linearly to a bath of harmonic oscillators, yielding controlled descriptions of friction, noise and decoherence.","Integrating out an oscillator environment produces an influence functional or reduced dynamics with dissipation and fluctuations tied to the bath spectrum.",["Caldeira Leggett","quantum Brownian motion","dissipation","environment"],[],"model"),
    T("anderson-impurity","Anderson impurity model",1961,"1960–1979","Quantum many-body & condensed matter","established model","The Anderson impurity model describes a localized interacting electronic orbital hybridized with a conduction band and underpins modern impurity and Kondo physics.","Competition among local Coulomb repulsion, orbital energy and hybridization generates local moments, charge fluctuations and correlated impurity behavior.",["Anderson impurity","Kondo","DMFT","correlations"],[],"model"),
    T("lieb-liniger","Lieb–Liniger model",1963,"1960–1979","Quantum many-body & condensed matter","established model","The Lieb–Liniger model is the exactly solvable one-dimensional Bose gas with contact interactions.","Bethe-ansatz rapidities encode the spectrum and interpolate between weakly interacting bosons and the strongly repulsive Tonks regime.",["Lieb Liniger","one dimension","Bethe ansatz","bosons"],[],"model"),
    T("tonks-girardeau","Tonks–Girardeau gas",1960,"1960–1979","Quantum many-body & condensed matter","established model","The Tonks–Girardeau limit describes one-dimensional bosons with infinitely strong short-range repulsion that map to noninteracting fermions for many observables.","Impenetrability enforces nodal structure allowing a Bose–Fermi mapping while retaining bosonic exchange symmetry.",["Tonks Girardeau","1D bosons","Bose Fermi mapping","strong interactions"],[],"model"),
    T("rokhsar-kivelson","Rokhsar–Kivelson quantum dimer model",1988,"1980–1999","Quantum many-body & condensed matter","established model","The quantum dimer model describes resonating hard-core dimer coverings on a lattice and provides a controlled route to valence-bond phases and quantum spin liquids.","Kinetic plaquette flips compete with potential energies for flippable dimers, with a solvable Rokhsar–Kivelson point separating phases in canonical cases.",["quantum dimer","Rokhsar Kivelson","spin liquid","valence bond"],[],"model"),
    T("syk-model","Sachdev–Ye–Kitaev model",1993,"1980–1999","Quantum many-body & condensed matter","active framework","The SYK family consists of strongly interacting all-to-all random fermion models with solvable large-N dynamics, maximal quantum chaos in a regime, and connections to holography.","Random many-fermion couplings generate a conformal low-energy regime with nontrivial entropy and characteristic chaotic correlation functions.",["SYK","quantum chaos","holography","strong correlations"],["Sachdev-Ye-Kitaev model"],"model"),
    T("gutzwiller-variational","Gutzwiller variational framework",1963,"1960–1979","Quantum many-body & condensed matter","established framework","The Gutzwiller approach uses correlated variational wavefunctions that suppress energetically costly local configurations relative to an uncorrelated reference state.","A local projection acting on a Slater determinant tunes double occupancy and captures key correlation effects near metal–insulator transitions.",["Gutzwiller","variational","Hubbard","correlations"],[],"many-body framework"),
    T("eliashberg-theory","Eliashberg strong-coupling superconductivity",1960,"1960–1979","Quantum many-body & condensed matter","established framework","Eliashberg theory extends BCS superconductivity to retarded, frequency-dependent electron–boson interactions and strong-coupling effects.","Self-consistent frequency-dependent gap and renormalization functions are determined from the bosonic spectral density and electronic interactions.",["Eliashberg","superconductivity","electron phonon","strong coupling"],[],"theory / framework"),
    T("nuclear-shell-model","Nuclear shell model",1949,"1940–1959","Nuclear quantum theory","established framework","The nuclear shell model describes protons and neutrons moving in quantized single-particle orbitals with residual interactions in a truncated valence space.","Magic numbers, spectra and transition properties emerge from shell structure plus configuration mixing among valence nucleons.",["nuclear shell model","nuclear structure","configuration interaction","magic numbers"],[],"many-body framework"),
    T("nuclear-collective-model","Nuclear collective model",1952,"1940–1959","Nuclear quantum theory","established framework","The Bohr–Mottelson collective model combines single-particle nuclear motion with collective rotations and vibrations of a deformable nucleus.","Quadrupole shape coordinates and rotational degrees of freedom organize low-energy spectra and electromagnetic transitions in deformed nuclei.",["Bohr Mottelson","collective model","nuclear rotation","vibration"],[],"many-body framework"),
    T("nuclear-dft","Nuclear density-functional theory",1970,"1960–1979","Nuclear quantum theory","established framework","Nuclear DFT describes nuclei through self-consistent energy-density functionals of nucleonic densities and currents, including symmetry-breaking mean fields and beyond-mean-field extensions.","An energy functional is minimized over quasiparticle or single-particle states to predict ground-state and collective nuclear observables across the chart.",["nuclear DFT","energy density functional","nuclear structure","mean field"],[],"computational framework"),
    T("nuclear-hfb","Nuclear Hartree–Fock–Bogoliubov theory",1960,"1960–1979","Nuclear quantum theory","established framework","Nuclear HFB theory treats self-consistent mean fields and pairing correlations simultaneously through quasiparticle states.","Particle–hole and particle–particle fields are solved together in a generalized density-matrix variational framework.",["HFB","pairing","nuclear structure","mean field"],[],"computational framework"),
    T("no-core-shell-model","No-core shell model",1998,"1980–1999","Nuclear quantum theory","established framework","The no-core shell model diagonalizes realistic nuclear Hamiltonians in large many-body oscillator spaces without assuming an inert core.","All nucleons are active, and convergence is controlled by systematic enlargement of the truncated basis together with effective or softened interactions.",["NCSM","ab initio","nuclear structure","shell model"],[],"computational framework"),
    T("in-medium-srg","In-medium similarity renormalization group",2011,"2000–2014","Nuclear quantum theory","established framework","The in-medium SRG continuously transforms nuclear Hamiltonians toward forms that decouple a chosen many-body reference space or valence space.","Flow equations suppress off-diagonal couplings while induced many-body operators are truncated in a controlled approximation hierarchy.",["IMSRG","similarity renormalization group","ab initio","nuclear structure"],[],"computational framework"),
    T("chiral-nuclear-eft","Chiral nuclear effective field theory",1990,"1980–1999","Nuclear quantum theory","established framework","Chiral nuclear EFT derives nucleon and pion interactions from the symmetries and symmetry-breaking pattern of low-energy QCD using an expansion in momenta and pion masses.","Power counting organizes two-, three- and higher-nucleon forces and consistent electroweak currents order by order below the chiral breakdown scale.",["chiral EFT","nuclear forces","QCD","few body"],[],"effective field theory"),
    T("pionless-nuclear-eft","Pionless nuclear EFT",1997,"1980–1999","Nuclear quantum theory","established framework","Pionless EFT describes very low-energy few-nucleon systems using contact interactions when pion exchange is unresolved.","Short-range operators are organized by power counting and nonperturbative resummation of leading interactions reproduces large scattering lengths and universal few-body behavior.",["pionless EFT","few nucleon","contact interaction","universality"],[],"effective field theory"),
    T("halo-eft","Halo effective field theory",2001,"2000–2014","Nuclear quantum theory","established framework","Halo EFT treats weakly bound nuclei as effective few-body systems composed of compact cores and halo nucleons at momentum scales below core excitation energies.","Low-energy observables are expanded in the ratio of halo to core scales using contact interactions and explicit halo degrees of freedom.",["halo EFT","halo nuclei","few body","effective theory"],[],"effective field theory"),
    T("relativistic-mean-field-nuclear","Relativistic mean-field nuclear theory",1974,"1960–1979","Nuclear quantum theory","established framework","Relativistic mean-field models describe nuclei and nuclear matter using Dirac nucleons interacting through classical meson or density-functional fields.","Large scalar and vector self-energies generate nuclear saturation and spin-orbit structure in a Lorentz-covariant mean-field description.",["relativistic mean field","Walecka","nuclear matter","covariant DFT"],[],"many-body framework"),
    T("parton-model","Parton model",1969,"1960–1979","Quantum field theory","historical framework","The parton model describes high-energy hadrons as collections of effectively pointlike constituents carrying fractions of the hadron momentum and provided the precursor language for quarks and gluons in QCD factorization.","Deep-inelastic scattering structure functions are interpreted in terms of incoherent scattering from fast constituents with momentum-fraction distributions.",["parton model","deep inelastic scattering","PDF","QCD"],[],"historical framework"),
    T("dglap-evolution","DGLAP evolution",1977,"1960–1979","Quantum field theory","established framework","DGLAP equations describe the scale dependence of collinear parton distribution and fragmentation functions in perturbative QCD.","Universal splitting kernels evolve parton densities with the logarithm of the hard scale by resumming leading collinear logarithms.",["DGLAP","parton distributions","QCD","evolution"],["Altarelli-Parisi evolution"],"theory / framework"),
    T("bfkl-evolution","BFKL high-energy evolution",1976,"1960–1979","Quantum field theory","established framework","BFKL evolution resums leading high-energy logarithms in perturbative QCD and governs gluon dynamics in the small-Bjorken-x regime before saturation effects dominate.","A transverse-momentum kernel evolves gluon exchange amplitudes with rapidity, generating characteristic small-x growth.",["BFKL","small x","QCD","Regge"],[],"theory / framework"),
    T("color-glass-condensate","Color Glass Condensate",1994,"1980–1999","Quantum field theory","active effective framework","The Color Glass Condensate is an effective field theory for high-density small-x gluons in energetic hadrons and nuclei where nonlinear saturation effects become important.","Fast color sources generate classical small-x gauge fields whose probability distribution evolves with energy through nonlinear renormalization-group equations.",["CGC","gluon saturation","small x","QCD"],[],"effective field theory"),
    T("qcd-sum-rules","QCD sum-rule framework",1979,"1960–1979","Quantum field theory","established framework","QCD sum rules relate short-distance operator-product expansions of current correlators to hadronic spectral information, incorporating vacuum condensates and quark–hadron duality assumptions.","Borel or moment transforms connect perturbative plus power-correction correlators to resonance parameters and continuum spectral models.",["QCD sum rules","SVZ","condensates","OPE"],[],"nonperturbative framework"),
    T("abj-anomaly","Adler–Bell–Jackiw chiral anomaly",1969,"1960–1979","Quantum field theory","established theorem","The ABJ anomaly shows that a classically conserved axial current acquires a quantum divergence in gauge theory through regularization of fermion loops.","Quantum effects break the classical axial symmetry, linking current nonconservation to gauge-field topology and physically observable processes.",["chiral anomaly","ABJ","topology","QFT"],[],"theorem"),
    T("yang-mills-instantons","Yang–Mills instantons and θ-vacuum",1975,"1960–1979","Quantum field theory","established framework","Yang–Mills instantons are finite-action Euclidean gauge configurations connecting topologically distinct vacua and underpin the θ-vacuum structure of non-Abelian gauge theory.","Gauge fields fall into topological sectors labeled by winding number, with tunneling amplitudes between sectors contributing nonperturbative effects.",["instantons","theta vacuum","Yang Mills","topology"],[],"nonperturbative framework"),
    T("gim-mechanism","GIM mechanism",1970,"1960–1979","Quantum field theory","established framework","The Glashow–Iliopoulos–Maiani mechanism suppresses flavor-changing neutral currents through the structure of quark weak interactions and motivated the charm quark.","Unitary mixing among quark weak doublets produces cancellations of neutral-current flavor change at tree level and strong loop suppression.",["GIM","flavor","weak interaction","charm"],[],"theory / framework"),
    T("ckm-mixing","CKM quark mixing and CP violation",1973,"1960–1979","Quantum field theory","established framework","The Cabibbo–Kobayashi–Maskawa framework describes charged-current flavor mixing among three quark generations and contains an irreducible complex phase that produces Standard Model CP violation.","A unitary three-generation mixing matrix rotates between quark mass and weak-interaction bases, with rephasing-invariant phase combinations governing CP-odd effects.",["CKM","CP violation","quark mixing","Standard Model"],[],"theory / framework"),
    T("operator-product-expansion","Operator product expansion",1969,"1960–1979","Quantum field theory","established framework","The operator product expansion expresses products of local operators at short separation as sums of local operators multiplied by scale-dependent coefficient functions.","Short-distance singular behavior is separated into Wilson coefficients while long-distance physics resides in matrix elements of local operators.",["OPE","Wilson coefficients","renormalization","QFT"],[],"formal framework"),
    T("einstein-cartan","Einstein–Cartan gravity",1922,"1900–1924","Quantum gravity & spacetime","established alternative gravity theory","Einstein–Cartan theory extends general relativity to an independent metric-compatible connection with torsion sourced algebraically by intrinsic spin.","Spin density couples to spacetime torsion, which vanishes outside spin-polarized matter in the simplest theory and modifies gravity at high densities.",["Einstein Cartan","torsion","spin","gravity"],[],"alternative theory"),
    T("teleparallel-gravity","Teleparallel equivalent of general relativity",1928,"1925–1939","Quantum gravity & spacetime","established reformulation","Teleparallel gravity reformulates general relativity using a curvature-free connection with torsion, encoding gravitational dynamics in torsion rather than Levi-Civita curvature.","A tetrad and flat affine connection define the torsion scalar whose action differs from the Einstein–Hilbert action by a boundary term in the equivalent theory.",["teleparallel","torsion","TEGR","gravity"],["TEGR"],"formulation"),
    T("f-t-gravity","f(T) teleparallel gravity",2011,"2000–2014","Quantum gravity & spacetime","active theory family","f(T) gravity generalizes teleparallel gravity by replacing the torsion scalar in the action with a nonlinear function.","Modified torsion dynamics add effective gravitational degrees of freedom and cosmological phenomenology distinct from curvature-based f(R) theories.",["f(T)","teleparallel","modified gravity","torsion"],[],"theory family"),
    T("lovelock-gravity","Lovelock gravity",1971,"1960–1979","Quantum gravity & spacetime","established gravity framework","Lovelock gravity is the most general metric theory in arbitrary dimension built from curvature tensors that yields second-order metric field equations for the Lovelock polynomial action.","Higher-dimensional Euler-density terms extend the Einstein–Hilbert action while avoiding generic higher-derivative equations of motion.",["Lovelock","higher curvature","Gauss Bonnet","gravity"],[],"theory family"),
    T("metric-affine-gravity","Metric-affine gravity",1976,"1960–1979","Quantum gravity & spacetime","active theory family","Metric-affine gravity treats the spacetime metric and affine connection as independent variables, allowing torsion and nonmetricity alongside curvature.","Matter hypermomentum can source connection degrees of freedom, unifying Riemannian, Einstein–Cartan, Weyl and broader affine geometries in one framework.",["metric affine","torsion","nonmetricity","gravity"],[],"theory family"),
    T("bimetric-gravity","Ghost-free bimetric gravity",2012,"2000–2014","Quantum gravity & spacetime","active research","Ghost-free bimetric gravity promotes both metrics of the dRGT interaction potential to dynamical fields while retaining the special nonlinear structure that removes the Boulware–Deser ghost.","Two interacting spin-2 sectors combine into massless and massive gravitational modes governed by the Hassan–Rosen potential.",["bimetric gravity","Hassan Rosen","massive gravity","spin 2"],[],"alternative theory"),
    T("double-field-theory","Double Field Theory",2009,"2000–2014","Quantum gravity & spacetime","active research","Double Field Theory makes string T-duality covariance manifest by doubling coordinates and organizing the massless closed-string sector using O(D,D) geometry.","A section constraint removes the redundant doubled dependence while generalized metric and dilaton fields encode conventional metric, B-field and dilaton data.",["double field theory","T duality","string theory","generalized geometry"],["DFT"],"theory / framework"),
    T("exceptional-field-theory","Exceptional Field Theory",2013,"2000–2014","Quantum gravity & spacetime","active research","Exceptional Field Theory extends duality-covariant reformulations to exceptional symmetry groups associated with M-theory and type-II supergravity compactifications.","Extended coordinates and generalized gauge symmetries make exceptional U-duality structures manifest subject to a section constraint.",["exceptional field theory","U duality","M theory","supergravity"],["ExFT"],"theory / framework"),
    T("circuit-model-qc","Quantum circuit model",1989,"1980–1999","Quantum information & open systems","established framework","The quantum circuit model represents quantum computation as sequences of local quantum gates acting on registers of qubits or qudits and is the standard framework for universal gate-based computation.","Unitary gates, ancillas and measurements compose finite-depth networks whose computational power is characterized by universal gate sets and complexity classes.",["quantum circuits","gate model","quantum computation","universal gates"],["gate-model quantum computation"],"computation framework"),
    T("quantum-turing-machine","Quantum Turing machine",1985,"1980–1999","Quantum information & open systems","established framework","The quantum Turing machine generalizes the classical Turing-machine model to coherent quantum transitions and supplied an early universal model of quantum computation.","A superposition of computational configurations evolves unitarily under local transition rules, enabling algorithms beyond classical probabilistic computation.",["quantum Turing machine","Deutsch","quantum computation","universality"],[],"computation framework"),
    T("quantum-walks","Quantum walks",1993,"1980–1999","Quantum information & open systems","established framework","Quantum walks are coherent quantum analogues of classical random walks with discrete- or continuous-time variants used in algorithms, transport and simulation.","Interfering amplitudes spread across graph vertices according to unitary walk dynamics rather than stochastic transition probabilities.",["quantum walk","quantum algorithms","transport","graphs"],[],"computation framework"),
    T("quantum-cellular-automata","Quantum cellular automata",1990,"1980–1999","Quantum information & open systems","active framework","Quantum cellular automata are spatially local, translation-structured unitary dynamics on quantum lattice systems and provide models for quantum computation, Floquet phases and discretized field theories.","Locality and finite information-propagation speed constrain a global reversible quantum update rule acting on lattice cells.",["QCA","quantum computation","lattice","Floquet"],[],"computation framework"),
    T("quantum-shannon-theory","Quantum Shannon theory",1995,"1980–1999","Quantum information & open systems","established framework","Quantum Shannon theory studies asymptotic rates for transmitting classical and quantum information and entanglement through noisy quantum channels.","Coding theorems define channel capacities, entanglement-assisted rates and trade-offs using entropic quantities and regularized resource rates.",["quantum Shannon theory","channel capacity","coding theorem","quantum communication"],[],"information-theoretic framework"),
    T("magic-state-theory","Magic-state resource theory",2005,"2000–2014","Quantum information & open systems","established framework","Magic-state theory quantifies nonstabilizer resources that enable universal fault-tolerant quantum computation beyond Clifford operations.","Special nonstabilizer states can be distilled and consumed to implement otherwise unavailable non-Clifford gates, with magic monotones quantifying the resource.",["magic states","stabilizer","fault tolerance","resource theory"],[],"resource framework"),
    T("relativistic-quantum-information","Relativistic quantum information",2003,"2000–2014","Quantum information & open systems","active research","Relativistic quantum information studies entanglement, communication and quantum protocols when observers, fields and reference frames are relativistic or live in curved spacetime.","Mode definitions, acceleration, horizons and spacetime structure alter operational access to quantum information and correlations.",["relativistic quantum information","entanglement","Unruh","curved spacetime"],[],"research framework"),
    T("boson-sampling","Boson sampling",2011,"2000–2014","Quantum information & open systems","established restricted model","Boson sampling is a restricted photonic computational model in which indistinguishable bosons propagate through a linear optical network and are sampled at the output.","Output probabilities are governed by matrix permanents, providing a route to quantum computational advantage without a universal gate model under standard complexity assumptions.",["boson sampling","linear optics","quantum advantage","permanent"],[],"computation framework"),

    T("kms-equilibrium","KMS equilibrium-state framework",1957,"1940–1959","Mathematical structures","established framework","The Kubo–Martin–Schwinger framework gives an operator-algebraic characterization of thermal equilibrium states for quantum systems, especially in the thermodynamic limit.","A state is thermal at inverse temperature β when correlation functions satisfy the KMS analyticity and imaginary-time boundary condition with respect to the dynamics.",["KMS","thermal equilibrium","operator algebra","statistical mechanics"],[],"mathematical framework"),
    T("kadanoff-baym","Kadanoff–Baym nonequilibrium Green-function theory",1962,"1960–1979","Quantum many-body & condensed matter","established framework","Kadanoff–Baym theory describes nonequilibrium interacting quantum systems through two-time Green functions and self-consistent collision integrals derived from many-body field theory.","Contour-ordered Dyson equations yield coupled evolution equations for correlation and spectral functions, bridging microscopic dynamics and quantum kinetic descriptions.",["Kadanoff Baym","nonequilibrium Green functions","quantum kinetics","many body"],[],"dynamical framework"),
    T("ginzburg-landau-superconductivity","Ginzburg–Landau superconductivity",1950,"1940–1959","Quantum many-body & condensed matter","established effective framework","Ginzburg–Landau theory describes superconductivity near a continuous transition using a complex order parameter coupled to the electromagnetic field.","A symmetry-constrained free-energy functional of the superconducting order parameter yields coherence, penetration and vortex physics at long wavelengths.",["Ginzburg Landau","superconductivity","order parameter","vortices"],[],"effective framework"),
    T("bogoliubov-de-gennes","Bogoliubov–de Gennes superconducting formalism",1958,"1940–1959","Quantum many-body & condensed matter","established framework","The Bogoliubov–de Gennes formalism describes quasiparticle excitations of spatially nonuniform superconductors in a particle–hole doubled mean-field representation.","A self-consistent pairing field enters a matrix eigenproblem coupling particle and hole amplitudes, resolving interfaces, vortices and inhomogeneous pairing.",["BdG","superconductivity","quasiparticles","pairing"],["Bogoliubov-de Gennes equations"],"many-body framework"),
    T("bcs-bec-crossover","BCS–BEC crossover framework",1980,"1980–1999","Quantum many-body & condensed matter","established framework","BCS–BEC crossover theory connects weakly bound Cooper-pair superconductivity or superfluidity continuously to Bose condensation of tightly bound pairs.","Changing interaction strength and chemical potential evolves fermionic pairing from large overlapping pairs to composite bosons without requiring a symmetry-changing phase transition in the simplest crossover.",["BCS BEC crossover","superfluidity","pairing","strong coupling"],[],"theory / framework"),
    T("entanglement-theory","Quantum entanglement theory",1996,"1980–1999","Quantum information & open systems","established framework","Entanglement theory classifies, detects, quantifies and manipulates nonseparable quantum correlations under specified classes of local operations and communication.","States are organized by convertibility under LOCC or related free operations, with entanglement measures and distillation/cost tasks characterizing the resource.",["entanglement","LOCC","resource theory","quantum information"],[],"resource framework"),
    T("quantum-simulation","Quantum simulation",1982,"1980–1999","Quantum information & open systems","established framework","Quantum simulation uses controllable quantum systems or quantum computers to emulate the dynamics and properties of other quantum systems that are difficult to calculate classically.","Analog or digital simulators encode a target Hamiltonian or evolution in an experimentally controllable quantum platform and extract observables from the simulator.",["quantum simulation","Feynman","analog quantum simulation","digital quantum simulation"],[],"computation framework"),
    T("black-hole-final-state","Black-hole final-state proposal",2004,"2000–2014","Quantum gravity & spacetime","speculative","The Horowitz–Maldacena proposal imposes a special final-state boundary condition at a black-hole singularity to reconcile Hawking evaporation with unitary quantum mechanics.","A maximally entangled final condition correlates infalling matter with interior Hawking partners so the outgoing radiation can encode the input state under idealized assumptions.",["black hole information","final state","Horowitz Maldacena","unitarity"],[],"research proposal"),
    T("black-hole-remnants","Black-hole remnant scenarios",1992,"1980–1999","Quantum gravity & spacetime","speculative","Black-hole remnant scenarios propose that evaporation halts near the Planck scale, leaving long-lived or stable objects that retain information otherwise lost in Hawking radiation.","A small final object is assumed to possess enough internal states or structure to encode the information of the original black hole, raising consistency questions about production and entropy.",["black hole information","remnant","evaporation","Planck scale"],[],"research program"),
    T("replica-wormholes","Replica-wormhole framework",2019,"2015–present","Quantum gravity & spacetime","active research","Replica-wormhole calculations include gravitational saddles connecting replica copies in entropy path integrals and reproduce Page-curve behavior in tractable semiclassical models.","New replica-connected geometries modify the semiclassical entropy calculation and lead to the island rule after analytic continuation in replica number.",["replica wormholes","Page curve","islands","black hole information"],[],"quantum-gravity framework"),
    T("starobinsky-inflation","Starobinsky R² inflation",1980,"1980–1999","Astroparticle physics & cosmology","established inflationary model","Starobinsky inflation uses higher-curvature R² dynamics to generate a quasi-de Sitter early universe and a predictive slow-roll inflationary regime.","The R+R² gravitational action is dynamically equivalent to Einstein gravity plus a scalaron with a plateau-like potential in the Einstein-frame description.",["Starobinsky","R2 inflation","scalaron","inflation"],[],"cosmological framework"),
    T("hybrid-inflation","Hybrid inflation",1991,"1980–1999","Astroparticle physics & cosmology","active inflationary model","Hybrid inflation uses at least two fields so inflation can proceed along a slowly varying direction and end through an instability of a second waterfall field.","The vacuum energy is maintained while the inflaton evolves until a critical value destabilizes the auxiliary field and terminates inflation rapidly.",["hybrid inflation","waterfall field","inflation","early universe"],[],"cosmological framework"),
    T("warm-inflation","Warm inflation",1995,"1980–1999","Astroparticle physics & cosmology","active inflationary framework","Warm inflation incorporates dissipative interactions during inflation so radiation can be continuously produced rather than appearing only after a separate reheating stage.","The inflaton equation includes a friction-like dissipation term and thermal fluctuations can contribute to primordial perturbations when the radiation bath is significant.",["warm inflation","dissipation","thermal fluctuations","inflation"],[],"cosmological framework"),
    T("k-essence","k-essence scalar-field cosmology",2000,"2000–2014","Astroparticle physics & cosmology","active framework","k-essence models use scalar fields with noncanonical kinetic terms to drive accelerated expansion or other cosmological dynamics.","A nonlinear function of the scalar kinetic invariant and field value produces an effective pressure and sound speed not obtainable from a canonical scalar field alone.",["k-essence","dark energy","noncanonical scalar","cosmology"],[],"cosmological framework"),
    T("symmetric-teleparallel-gravity","Symmetric teleparallel gravity",2018,"2015–present","Quantum gravity & spacetime","active research","Symmetric teleparallel gravity describes gravitation using nonmetricity in a geometry with vanishing curvature and torsion, providing a third geometric formulation alongside curvature and torsion descriptions.","A flat torsion-free affine connection carries nonmetricity, and the equivalent GR action is built from a specific quadratic nonmetricity scalar plus a boundary relation.",["symmetric teleparallel","nonmetricity","gravity","coincident gauge"],[],"formulation"),
    T("f-q-gravity","f(Q) gravity",2018,"2015–present","Quantum gravity & spacetime","active theory family","f(Q) gravity generalizes symmetric teleparallel gravity by replacing the nonmetricity scalar Q in the action with a nonlinear function.","Nonlinear nonmetricity dynamics modify the gravitational field equations and provide cosmological and astrophysical alternatives distinct from f(R) and f(T) families.",["f(Q)","nonmetricity","modified gravity","symmetric teleparallel"],[],"theory family"),

    T("nonmarkovian-open-systems","Non-Markovian open quantum dynamics",1960,"1960–1979","Quantum information & open systems","established framework","Non-Markovian open-system theory describes reduced quantum dynamics with memory, information backflow or other departures from dynamical-semigroup behavior.","System evolution depends on environmental correlations and prior history, requiring structures beyond a time-independent GKSL generator.",["non-Markovian","memory","open systems","information backflow"],[],"dynamical framework"),
    T("nakajima-zwanzig","Nakajima–Zwanzig projection-operator formalism",1958,"1940–1959","Quantum information & open systems","established framework","The Nakajima–Zwanzig formalism projects full Liouville dynamics onto chosen relevant degrees of freedom and yields exact generalized master equations with memory kernels.","Projection superoperators separate relevant and irrelevant sectors, producing an integro-differential reduced equation whose memory kernel encodes eliminated dynamics.",["Nakajima Zwanzig","projection operator","memory kernel","open systems"],[],"formal framework"),
    T("bloch-redfield","Bloch–Redfield master-equation theory",1957,"1940–1959","Quantum information & open systems","established approximation","Bloch–Redfield theory derives weak-coupling reduced dynamics from system–bath correlation functions without imposing the full secular approximation required for GKSL form.","A perturbative relaxation tensor governs density-matrix evolution and can retain coherences and frequency couplings that are discarded by stronger Markovian approximations.",["Redfield","master equation","relaxation","open systems"],["Redfield equation"],"dynamical framework"),
    T("heom","Hierarchical equations of motion",1989,"1980–1999","Quantum information & open systems","established computational framework","HEOM represents non-Markovian reduced dynamics through a hierarchy of coupled auxiliary density operators, enabling numerically exact treatment for important classes of Gaussian environments.","A decomposed bath correlation function generates tiered auxiliary operators whose coupled equations retain environmental memory and strong system–bath effects.",["HEOM","non-Markovian","open systems","numerically exact"],[],"computational framework"),
    T("weak-measurement","Weak measurement and weak-value formalism",1988,"1980–1999","Foundations & interpretations","established measurement framework","Weak-measurement theory describes minimally disturbing measurements on pre- and postselected ensembles and introduces weak values that can lie outside an observable's eigenvalue range.","A weak system–pointer coupling followed by postselection yields a pointer shift governed, to leading order, by a complex transition-amplitude ratio called the weak value.",["weak measurement","weak value","postselection","Aharonov"],[],"measurement framework"),
    T("no-broadcasting","No-broadcasting theorem",1996,"1980–1999","Foundations & interpretations","established theorem","The no-broadcasting theorem extends no-cloning to mixed states by showing that a set of quantum states can be broadcast exactly only when the relevant states commute.","Generic noncommuting density operators cannot be copied into two subsystems while reproducing the original state in both marginals.",["no broadcasting","no cloning","mixed states","quantum information"],[],"theorem"),
    T("cpt-theorem","CPT theorem",1954,"1940–1959","Quantum field theory","established theorem","The CPT theorem states that local Lorentz-invariant quantum field theories satisfying standard assumptions are invariant under the combined action of charge conjugation, parity and time reversal.","The structural assumptions of relativistic local QFT enforce an exact combined CPT symmetry even when C, P or T are separately violated.",["CPT","Lorentz invariance","locality","QFT"],[],"theorem"),
    T("spin-statistics-theorem","Spin–statistics theorem",1940,"1940–1959","Quantum field theory","established theorem","The spin–statistics theorem links integer-spin fields with Bose statistics and half-integer-spin fields with Fermi statistics under relativistic locality and positivity assumptions.","Relativistic quantum theory cannot consistently assign ordinary bosonic statistics to half-integer spin or fermionic statistics to integer spin while retaining the theorem's assumptions.",["spin statistics","bosons","fermions","QFT"],[],"theorem"),
    T("haag-theorem","Haag's theorem",1955,"1940–1959","Quantum field theory","established no-go theorem","Haag's theorem shows that under the axioms of relativistic QFT an interacting field cannot be related to a free field by the unitary interaction-picture transformation assumed in naive canonical perturbation theory.","The free and interacting representations are generally unitarily inequivalent in the continuum theory, exposing why renormalized QFT cannot literally realize the textbook interaction picture.",["Haag theorem","interaction picture","axiomatic QFT","no-go"],[],"theorem"),
    T("coleman-mandula","Coleman–Mandula theorem",1967,"1960–1979","Quantum field theory","established theorem","The Coleman–Mandula theorem strongly restricts nontrivial combinations of spacetime and internal symmetries for an interacting relativistic S-matrix under stated assumptions.","Ordinary Lie symmetries of a nontrivial relativistic S-matrix factor into Poincaré and internal parts, with supersymmetry later providing a graded-symmetry evasion.",["Coleman Mandula","symmetry","S matrix","supersymmetry"],[],"theorem"),
    T("weinberg-witten","Weinberg–Witten theorem",1980,"1980–1999","Quantum field theory","established theorem","The Weinberg–Witten theorem constrains massless particles of sufficiently high spin in theories possessing Lorentz-covariant conserved currents or stress tensors.","Under its assumptions, certain composite or emergent massless charged particles and massless spin-two states cannot carry the relevant Lorentz-covariant conserved quantities.",["Weinberg Witten","massless particles","emergent gravity","no-go"],[],"theorem"),
    T("goldstone-theorem","Goldstone theorem",1961,"1960–1979","Quantum field theory","established theorem","Goldstone's theorem relates spontaneous breaking of continuous global symmetries to massless excitation modes in relativistic field theory under the theorem's assumptions.","A vacuum that breaks a continuous global symmetry supports gapless Nambu–Goldstone modes associated with the broken generators.",["Goldstone","spontaneous symmetry breaking","Nambu Goldstone","QFT"],[],"theorem"),
    T("fermi-four-fermion","Fermi four-fermion theory of beta decay",1934,"1925–1939","Quantum field theory","historical effective theory","Fermi's beta-decay theory models the weak interaction as a local four-fermion contact interaction and is the historical prototype of a low-energy effective field theory.","Nuclear beta decay is described by a pointlike interaction among hadronic and leptonic currents, valid at energies far below the weak-boson mass scale.",["Fermi theory","beta decay","weak interaction","EFT"],[],"effective field theory"),
    T("va-weak-theory","V–A theory of weak interactions",1958,"1940–1959","Quantum field theory","historical framework","The vector-minus-axial-vector theory identified the chiral current structure of charged weak interactions prior to the electroweak gauge theory.","Weak charged currents couple left-handed fermionic components through a universal V–A four-fermion interaction at low energy.",["V-A","weak interaction","parity violation","Feynman Gell-Mann"],[],"theory / framework"),
    T("unimodular-gravity","Unimodular gravity",1919,"1900–1924","Quantum gravity & spacetime","active alternative gravity framework","Unimodular gravity restricts the metric determinant or equivalent volume element, yielding trace-free gravitational field equations with the cosmological constant arising as an integration constant in classical formulations.","Volume-preserving diffeomorphism structure changes how the cosmological constant enters the equations while classical local dynamics can coincide with general relativity under standard conservation assumptions.",["unimodular gravity","cosmological constant","volume preserving","gravity"],[],"alternative theory"),
    T("conformal-gravity","Weyl / conformal gravity",1918,"1900–1924","Quantum gravity & spacetime","active alternative gravity framework","Conformal gravity uses a Weyl-tensor-squared action invariant under local metric rescalings and yields fourth-order Bach equations rather than Einstein's second-order equations.","Local conformal symmetry replaces the Einstein–Hilbert scale with a dimensionless higher-curvature gravitational action.",["conformal gravity","Weyl gravity","scale invariance","higher derivative"],["Weyl gravity"],"alternative theory"),
    T("mimetic-gravity","Mimetic gravity",2013,"2000–2014","Quantum gravity & spacetime","active research","Mimetic gravity rewrites the physical metric in terms of an auxiliary metric and constrained scalar degree of freedom, making a conformal mode dynamical and allowing effective dark-sector behavior.","A noninvertible metric parametrization introduces a constrained scalar mode that can mimic cold dark matter and has spawned broader modified-gravity extensions.",["mimetic gravity","dark matter","conformal mode","modified gravity"],[],"theory family"),
    T("phantom-dark-energy","Phantom dark-energy models",2002,"2000–2014","Astroparticle physics & cosmology","speculative framework","Phantom dark-energy models have an effective equation-of-state parameter below minus one and can drive super-accelerated expansion, often at the cost of unusual kinetic structure or stability concerns.","An effective component with pressure more negative than its energy density evolves differently from a cosmological constant and can lead to future singular behavior in simple realizations.",["phantom energy","dark energy","w<-1","cosmology"],[],"cosmological framework"),
    T("chaplygin-gas","Chaplygin-gas cosmology",2001,"2000–2014","Astroparticle physics & cosmology","active phenomenological framework","Chaplygin-gas models use an exotic fluid with negative pressure inversely related to energy density to interpolate between matter-like and dark-energy-like behavior.","The fluid equation of state produces dust-like evolution at high density and accelerated expansion at low density in generalized variants.",["Chaplygin gas","dark energy","unified dark sector","cosmology"],[],"cosmological framework"),
    T("matter-bounce","Matter-bounce cosmology",1999,"1980–1999","Astroparticle physics & cosmology","active research","Matter-bounce scenarios replace an inflationary beginning with a contracting matter-dominated phase followed by a nonsingular bounce, generating nearly scale-invariant perturbations in canonical implementations.","Cosmological modes exit the shrinking Hubble radius during matter contraction and are transferred through a bounce into the expanding universe.",["matter bounce","bouncing cosmology","early universe","alternative to inflation"],[],"cosmological framework"),

    T("no-cloning","No-cloning theorem",1982,"1980–1999","Foundations & interpretations","established theorem","The no-cloning theorem proves that an arbitrary unknown quantum state cannot be perfectly copied by a universal physical operation.","Linearity and unitarity prevent one state-independent transformation from producing two identical copies of every possible input state.",["no cloning","quantum information","linearity","no-go theorem"],[],"theorem"),

    T("mackey-imprimitivity","Mackey imprimitivity framework",1949,"1940–1959","Mathematical structures","established theorem/framework","Mackey's imprimitivity theory links unitary group representations, covariance and projection-valued measures, providing a systematic representation-theoretic foundation for quantum observables with symmetry.","Systems of imprimitivity encode a group action together with covariant spectral measures and are classified through induced representations under the theorem's assumptions.",["Mackey","imprimitivity","induced representations","symmetry"],["Mackey imprimitivity theorem"],"theorem"),
    T("ludwig-operational-qm","Ludwig operational quantum mechanics",1964,"1960–1979","Foundations & interpretations","established axiomatic framework","Ludwig's operational program reconstructs quantum theory from preparations, registration procedures, ensembles, effects and empirically motivated axioms.","Operationally defined preparations and effects are organized into convex structures from which Hilbert-space quantum mechanics and measurement rules can be derived under additional assumptions.",["Ludwig","operational quantum theory","preparations","effects"],[],"axiomatic framework"),
    T("stone-von-neumann","Stone–von Neumann uniqueness theorem",1930,"1925–1939","Mathematical structures","established theorem","The Stone–von Neumann theorem establishes uniqueness, up to unitary equivalence, of irreducible regular representations of the canonical commutation relations for finitely many degrees of freedom.","Under continuity and irreducibility assumptions, the Weyl form of the canonical commutation relations has the Schrödinger representation as its unique representation class.",["Stone von Neumann","canonical commutation relations","representation theory","quantization"],[],"theorem"),
    T("wigner-symmetry-theorem","Wigner symmetry theorem",1931,"1925–1939","Mathematical structures","established theorem","Wigner's theorem shows that transformations of pure quantum states preserving transition probabilities are represented on Hilbert space by unitary or antiunitary operators.","A ray-space symmetry that preserves transition probabilities lifts to a linear unitary or antilinear antiunitary transformation of state vectors.",["Wigner theorem","symmetry","unitary","antiunitary"],[],"theorem"),
    T("reeh-schlieder","Reeh–Schlieder theorem",1961,"1960–1979","Quantum field theory","established theorem","The Reeh–Schlieder theorem states that the vacuum is cyclic for the algebra of observables associated with any nonempty open region in relativistic QFT under standard axiomatic assumptions.","Local field operations acting on the vacuum generate a dense set of states, revealing the deeply nonlocal entanglement structure of the QFT vacuum without enabling superluminal signalling.",["Reeh Schlieder","AQFT","vacuum entanglement","locality"],[],"theorem"),
    T("sine-gordon","Quantum sine-Gordon model",1975,"1960–1979","Quantum field theory","established integrable model","The quantum sine-Gordon model is a two-dimensional interacting scalar field theory with a periodic cosine potential, solitons and exact integrable structure.","Its soliton sector is nonperturbatively related to the massive Thirring model, making bosonization and particle–soliton duality explicit.",["sine-Gordon","integrable QFT","soliton","bosonization"],[],"model"),
    T("nonlinear-sigma-model","Nonlinear sigma model",1961,"1960–1979","Quantum field theory","established theory family","Nonlinear sigma models describe fields valued in a curved target manifold or constrained order-parameter space and form a central class of QFT and statistical-field models.","Derivative interactions determined by target-space geometry generate renormalization, topology and in two dimensions asymptotically free behavior for important O(N) cases.",["nonlinear sigma model","O(N)","asymptotic freedom","topology"],[],"theory family"),
    T("f-theory","F-theory",1996,"1980–1999","Quantum gravity & spacetime","active research","F-theory geometrizes the varying axio-dilaton of type-IIB string theory using elliptically fibered geometry and provides a nonperturbative framework for string compactifications.","An auxiliary elliptic fiber encodes SL(2,Z) duality data of type-IIB backgrounds, enabling compactifications with seven-branes and links to M-theory.",["F-theory","type IIB","elliptic fibration","string duality"],[],"research program"),
    T("ds-cft","dS/CFT correspondence",2001,"2000–2014","Quantum gravity & spacetime","active research","The dS/CFT proposal seeks a holographic relation between quantum gravity in de Sitter space and a conformal field theory associated with its asymptotic boundary.","Bulk de Sitter observables or wavefunction data are mapped to boundary conformal quantities, with important differences from the better-established AdS/CFT dictionary.",["dS/CFT","de Sitter","holography","CFT"],[],"research program"),
    T("liouville-quantum-gravity","Liouville quantum gravity",1981,"1980–1999","Quantum gravity & spacetime","established two-dimensional framework","Liouville quantum gravity describes fluctuating two-dimensional geometry through Liouville field theory and is central to noncritical string theory and rigorous random geometry.","The conformal factor of a two-dimensional metric becomes a quantum Liouville field whose coupling to matter encodes the path integral over random geometries.",["Liouville","2D quantum gravity","random geometry","noncritical string"],[],"quantum-gravity framework")
